jobs.description:
The Role

At Treewalk, you’ll own the entire public-company reporting cycle: fast closes, MD&A storytelling, IFRS/US GAAP judgment calls, and scalable system design. You’ll own end-to-end financial disclosure for a portfolio of high growth clients in life sciences, including pharmaceuticals, therapeutics, and other applications of biosciences and biotechnology. Many engagements will tap you as a de-facto fractional CFO, guiding strategy as well as disclosure; others will lean on you as the go-to technical expert. Either way, every file is yours to run.

Deadlines are real; overtime isn’t a lifestyle. We staff sensibly, treat extra hours as the rare exception, and back that up with true schedule autonomy and remote flexibility—so your evenings stay yours.

If you’ve led pub-co audits at a small- to mid-size firm or managed reporting inside a listed issuer, and you’re ready to trade 70-hour busy-season marathons for high-impact work, tangible ownership, and genuine balance, then we would love to hear from you.

How You’ll Create Impact Day-to-Day

  • Own the story behind the numbers: Draft and polish quarterly and annual financial statements and MD&A that stand up to capital-markets scrutiny and tell each client’s growth narrative from the science, to the milestones, and the financial commitments required to achieve the business objectives.
  • Make R&D spend make sense: Advise clients on accounting for research and development costs, clinical and pre-clinical trial accruals, CRO/CDMO arrangements, and measuring burn rate against progress.
  • Master the technical hurdles: Tackle complex issues such as licensing and collaboration agreements, milestone and royalty revenue, acquired IPR&D, government grants and funding, intangible assets and impairment, and package them into robust technical memos and disclosures.
  • Untangle complex capital structures: Work through warrants, convertible instruments, derivative liabilities, royalty and streaming financings, unit offerings, debt/equity splits, and stock-based compensation.
  • Run the engine of multi-entity groups: Build rock-solid consolidation and foreign-currency translation models that make complex structures look effortless.
  • Turn data into insight: Deliver sharp balance sheet and P&L analyses, spotlighting trends and red-flag variances before anyone else sees them.
  • Keep leadership laser-focused: Produce monthly variance reports against forecasts and annual plans, translating the findings into clear, action-ready recommendations, including cash runway and financing timing.
  • Shape the roadmap: Guide annual budgets and rolling forecasts, aligning stakeholders around targets that push the business without breaking it.
  • Step in as the “extra brain”: Handle special-project bookkeeping or period-end close entries when clients need a fractional controller’s precision and speed.
  • Make audits painless: Design year-end audit plans, prep airtight support, and quarterback conversations with external auditors so CEOs and CFOs can sleep at night.
  • Guard continuous disclosure: Stay ahead of regulatory changes, draft timely filings, and ensure nothing slips through the cracks on SEDAR+ or EDGAR.
  • Build and grow the industry service line: Take ownership of the practice area and scale it, and develop the people who will run alongside you.

Result: clients see you as the calm, expert voice who keeps them compliant and strategic, while you build Treewalk’s Biotechnology and Life Sciences service line without the grind of traditional public practice.

Requirements

Our ideal candidate...

  • CPA designation required.
  • Significant public company audit and/or financial reporting experience, serving or working within pre-revenue or early-commercial biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or other life sciences reporting issuers listed in Canada and/or the US.
  • Hands-on technical depth in life sciences accounting and fluency in the drug and product development lifecycle.
  • After the base experience requirements are met, we hire first and foremost for strong analytical and problem-solving skills.


Why Treewalk Feels Different

It’s Treewalk for a reason: we invest in your growth, trust your judgment, and protect your life outside the ledger.

  • No-Strings Learning Fund: We pay 100% of your CPA modules, annual dues, and any pro-dev courses you choose, and we’ll never claw it back if you move on.
  • Freedom Over Face-Time: Own your deadlines, shape your schedule. Hit a midday workout, do the school run. Just bring the results.
  • Day-One Peace of Mind: Extended health, dental, vision, and parental-leave benefits start the moment you join.

Benefits

Who We Are

Treewalk is Vancouver-born, scaling nationwide, and obsessed with turning capital-markets complexity into clarity. We give TSX, TSX-V, CSE, NASDAQ, and OTC issuers an end-to-end disclosure engine, so they can focus on growth while we keep them bullet-proof in the spotlight.

But labels like “accounting firm” don’t capture our DNA. Picture a tech startup powered by CPAs:

  • Holacracy over hierarchy: Ideas outrank titles, and ownership lives on every desk.
  • Sector depth, startup curiosity: If it’s innovative, we’re already in it, or will be tomorrow.
  • Growth at warp speed: One of Canada’s fastest-rising advisory practices, we set audacious goals, then sprint past them.
  • Training ground for tomorrow’s CFOs: Whether you’re a seasoned audit manager or a life sciences controller, Treewalk is where accountants level up for industry roles and capital-markets strategy.

The Values That Power Us

Mastery: We hunt knowledge relentlessly and build expertise into every engagement.
Support: No one goes it alone. Collaboration is our default setting.
Ownership: We celebrate wins and own slip-ups with equal conviction.
Kaizen: Continuous improvement isn’t a buzzword; it’s our daily operating system.

Annual Salary: $125,000

We are looking for a senior, hands-on software engineer who has used AI coding agents to deliver secure, production-ready software within established enterprise environments. Deliver production software. Personally design, implement, test, review and release agent-assisted changes to existing enterprise applications, not only new builds or prototypes.

  • Engineer agent workflows and harnesses. Build reusable instructions, tools, context pipelines, execution loops and feedback mechanisms that help agents work reliably within enterprise repositories and engineering controls.

You are a hands-on, security-conscious engineer who enjoys complex, imperfect codebases. You modernise existing systems safely, teach others by example and know when agents require human oversight. You are practical, collaborative and accountable for production quality.

Sobre nosotros

Draftea es la startup de tecnología mexicana que está revolucionando el mundo de las apuestas. Creada por y para los aficionados a los deportes, estamos respaldados por inversionistas de clase mundial como Sequoia, Kaszek y Bullpen. Nuestra razón de ser es sencilla: darle a los aficionados una nueva forma de disfrutar su pasión. Queremos que todos los amantes de los deportes puedan sentir como si cada partido fuera la final del mundial y cada triunfo una razón para celebrar. Queremos acercar a nuestros jugadores a sus ídolos y equipos y hacerlos partícipes de las emociones que se viven dentro del campo.

Además, deben tener una sólida comprensión de los productos y servicios de su empresa para abordar las preguntas de los clientes. También debe tener una actitud agradable y capacidad de negociación.

  • Resolución de problemas complejos, colaborar con los equipos internos con la finalidad de llegar a una solución para satisfacer las necesidades de nuestros clientes.

jobs.title: Recruiting Manager
jobs.excerpt: Do you think hiring should feel like a conversation, not a stack of applications?
jobs.description:
Do you think hiring should feel like a conversation, not a stack of applications?

Are you energized by running a hiring process that has to hit a spring peak and still treat every candidate like a person?

Do you get more out of a sharp intake meeting with a hiring manager than out of a full inbox?

Collegewise is looking for a Recruiting Manager to join our People team. This role owns hiring from the first conversation with a hiring manager through the moment a candidate accepts an offer, across counselors, program advisors, sales and marketing, and corporate and senior roles. It's hands-on work. You'll source, screen, interview, and close, while building the systems that keep the process running. This is a remote position, and candidates must be located in the United States.

Who We Are

Collegewise is a college counseling company that helps high school students confidently navigate their journey to college. We believe the college admissions process has spun out of control, with too much confusion, too much anxiety, and too many students losing agency for what should be their path to higher education. We’re out to change all that.

Since 1999, we’ve helped more than 35,000 students apply and get accepted to schools—sometimes famous, often not—that they’re excited to attend. We do it all with just the right mix of advice, encouragement, and occasional cheerleading—all backed by data and experience—to ensure that each student’s college admissions process runs smoothly and thoughtfully. And our work doesn’t stop with students who enroll in our program. We speak in public, write, and constantly look for ways to spread relevant college planning information to anyone who needs it, whether or not they work with us. To learn more about Collegewise, check out this short video.

Ambition with heart. Strategy with soul.

Yes, we're a business. But students come first, and that's never up for debate. We have an excellent reputation with both high school counselors and admissions officers. We present at NACAC, local ACACs, and at high schools and community events. We partner with community-based organizations to directly support their students and increase college access. We tell the truth, we treat people right, we recycle, and we have at least five confirmed vegetarians on the team. We're biased, but really, this is a pretty great place to work.

What's the Job?

Every hiring need starts with a conversation. A hiring manager needs a wave of counselors ahead of the spring peak, or one senior hire who has to be right. You'll sit down with that manager, get clear on the scope, scorecard, and timeline, and turn it into a job req and posting the team can act on.

From there, you run the process. You'll write external postings, build sourcing plans for core, specialist, and boutique counselors, program advisors, sales and marketing, and corporate roles, and keep a talent pool warm between hiring peaks. You'll lead hiring for program advisors, who build the trust families need to commit to a customized counseling and tutoring package. You'll run screening and interviews through to offer, draft and track offers within approved pay bands, and keep candidates informed until they accept.

The process itself is yours to design. You'll shape the screening criteria our counseling volunteers use, partner with Counseling leadership on how that training gets delivered, and own our employee referral program and the recruiting metrics that show whether hiring is working. You'll run Rippling as our applicant tracking system, including stages, scorecards, scheduling, and reporting. You'll also mentor and develop a part-time Recruiting Coordinator.

The hard part is making sure hiring managers get enough from each interview to decide. When they don't, you find out why and get them what they need, without losing the human side of the process. You'll work alongside our Chief People Officer, who approves job descriptions, senior and corporate hires, and pay bands. You make sure the people making those calls have what they need.

Who We're Looking For (You)

You run hiring like it matters, because it does. You make work a way of life without making it your actual life. You win people over quickly and earn trust fast, which matters when you're asking a candidate to bet on us.

The ideal candidate has some of the following experience, but probably not all. We get it.

  • You've run full-cycle recruiting on your own, owning requisitions from intake through offer acceptance.
  • You've recruited for multiple role types, including at least one of education, sales, or hourly and high-volume hiring.
  • You source hands-on: boolean search, outbound outreach, and building pipelines, not only reviewing inbound applicants.
  • You administer an ATS yourself, including workflows, scorecards, scheduling, and reporting.
  • You write and track offers within approved pay bands, and you know pay transparency rules and EEO and ADA interview practice.
  • You have full-cycle recruiting experience in education, healthcare, or another high-touch field.
  • You've managed a recruiting coordinator or other support staff.
  • You've managed an external recruiter or agency.

Most importantly, you believe in the vision of Collegewise. Every student we work with depends on the people we hire, and you'll help make sure we hire the right ones.

Work Life at Collegewise

We've worked hard to create the company we'd want to work for, with a culture that draws smart, fascinating professionals united by a desire to do the best work of our careers. For more information about our benefits and our approach to work, check outour Careers page.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: $80,000-85,000 per year
  • Employment Type: Full-time, salaried
  • Benefits: Full medical, dental, and vision coverage; paid parental leave; 401(k) with matching; and generous vacation and sick day policies.
  • Start Date: December or January
  • Location: Remote, US-based

How to Apply

Instead of a traditional cover letter, please choose 3 of the following questions to answer (150–250 words is a helpful guideline, but use as much or as little space as you need).

Application questions (choose 3):

  1. Why recruiting, and why Collegewise? Tell us what draws you to this work and our team specifically.
  2. Walk us through how you'd source for a role you've never filled before. Where would you look first, and how would you know it was working?
  3. Walk us through a time you used data to change a hiring decision. What did the numbers show, and what did you do with them?
  4. Describe how you've developed someone who supports your recruiting work. What did you hand off, what did you keep, and how did you know they were ready for more?
  5. A candidate you really want asks for more than we can offer. What do you do next, and how do you keep them engaged while you work it out?
  6. Tell us about a week when three or more open roles competed for the same time and attention. What did you drop, what did you protect, and how did you tell hiring managers?

Please submit your resume and responses through ourCareers page. Every single applicant will receive a response from us, and we do our very best to reply within 10 days.

We Want to Hear from You

Job Title: Vendor Scoping Lead - EMEA FSP

Job Location: Reading, Berkshire, United Kingdom

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Vendor Scoping Lead


Job Overview

The Vendor Scoping Lead is responsible for leading the end-to-end vendor scoping, budgeting, and outsourcing strategy process across clinical development programs. This role partners closely with Clinical Operations, Compound Operational Leads (COLs), Study Teams, Procurement, Finance, and external service providers to ensure accurate study cost forecasting, competitive vendor selection, and timely governance approvals.

The Vendor Scoping Lead plays a critical role in optimizing study delivery by balancing quality, timelines, and cost considerations while ensuring alignment with organizational outsourcing strategies and business objectives. The position requires strong expertise in clinical trial budgeting, financial modeling, vendor negotiations, and outsourcing governance across global clinical development programs.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end vendor scoping, budgeting, and outsourcing activities for global and regional clinical development programs.
  • Partner with study teams and key stakeholders to identify outsourcing requirements and develop fit-for-purpose vendor engagement strategies.
  • Develop, review, and optimize study budgets, ensuring accuracy, competitiveness, and alignment with program objectives.
  • Prepare cost scenarios, budget comparisons, and financial analyses to support governance discussions and decision-making.
  • Lead vendor budget negotiations and commercial discussions to achieve optimal value while maintaining quality and delivery standards.
  • Coordinate and support the preparation of Requests for Proposal (RFPs), bid evaluations, and vendor selection activities.
  • Evaluate vendor proposals, challenge assumptions, benchmark costs, and identify opportunities for budget optimization.
  • Collaborate with Procurement and Contract Services teams to ensure seamless transition from approved scope and budget to executed agreements.
  • Support study teams through governance review processes by preparing clear scoping documentation, financial analyses, and recommendation packages.
  • Monitor alignment between approved study scope, vendor proposals, and contractual commitments.
  • Contribute to the evaluation and management of preferred vendor relationships and strategic outsourcing partnerships.
  • Maintain awareness of market trends, vendor capabilities, outsourcing models, and industry benchmarking data.
  • Ensure appropriate balance between cost, timelines, quality, and operational feasibility throughout the vendor scoping process.
  • Act as a key point of contact between internal stakeholders and external service providers during planning and start-up phases.

Qualifications

Required Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Business Administration, Finance, Supply Chain, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, or clinical research environments.
  • At least 4 years of direct experience in clinical operations, vendor management, outsourcing, procurement, strategic sourcing, financial planning, or study budgeting.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting vendor selection, RFP management, scope development, and contract budgeting activities.
  • Experience negotiating budgets and commercial terms with CROs, central laboratories, clinical technology vendors, and other clinical service providers.
  • Strong understanding of clinical trial outsourcing models, governance structures, and drug development processes.
  • Experience preparing business cases, governance materials, and financial analyses for senior stakeholders.
  • Knowledge of clinical development across multiple phases and therapeutic areas is preferred.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong clinical trial budgeting and financial management expertise.
  • Advanced cost modelling, forecasting, and scenario analysis skills.
  • Ability to evaluate vendor proposals and translate operational needs into appropriate outsourcing scope.
  • Strong negotiation and influencing capabilities.
  • Excellent business acumen and commercial mindset.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills.
  • Ability to balance cost, quality, risk, and timelines when making recommendations.
  • Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Excellent communication and presentation abilities.
  • High attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
  • Demonstrated accountability, results orientation, agility, and continuous improvement mindset.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including advanced Excel skills.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English; additional languages are advantageous.

Preferred Background

Candidates may come from roles such as:

  • Vendor Scoping Lead
  • Clinical Vendor Manager
  • Outsourcing Manager
  • Strategic Sourcing Manager, Clinical Development
  • Clinical Procurement Manager
  • Clinical Finance Manager
  • Clinical Operations Manager
  • Vendor Relationship Manager
  • Clinical Trial Budget Manager
  • Study Start-Up and Outsourcing Lead

This position offers the opportunity to influence the financial and operational success of global clinical development programs through strategic vendor engagement, robust budgeting practices, and effective outsourcing leadership.

For more information on DTiQ visit our website () or our LinkedIn page ().

Role Overview
DTiQ is seeking a customer-focused, commercially minded Customer Experience professional to support the growth and success of DriveThruIQ across the Americas.
This role is responsible for ensuring customers successfully adopt, realize value from, and expand their use of DTiQ's Drive-Thru solutions. Working closely with Sales, Account Executives, Product, Technical Support, and Operations, the CX resource will support customer engagement throughout the customer lifecycle, from solution demonstrations and validation through deployment, adoption, retention, and expansion.
The role will play a critical part in supporting new business opportunities, demonstrating the operational value of DriveThruIQ, and ensuring customers achieve measurable outcomes from their investment.
The successful candidate will combine strong customer engagement skills with an understanding of QSR operations, technology adoption, and the commercial drivers behind customer retention and growth.
Key Responsibilities
1. Pre-Sales Support & Solution Validation
  • Partner with the Senior Director of Sales and Account Executives to support qualified DriveThruIQ opportunities.
  • Deliver product demonstrations and solution walkthroughs tailored to customer requirements.
  • Translate customer challenges into relevant product capabilities and operational outcomes.
  • Support technical validation, proof-of-concept activities, and pilot programs.
  • Engage Product and Technical teams to address solution questions and ensure customer expectations are aligned.
  • Develop the capability to independently lead standard demonstrations and validation activities, escalating strategic or complex opportunities to global CX leadership when required.
2. Customer Onboarding & Adoption
  • Support a structured handover from Sales into deployment and Customer Experience.
  • Coordinate with Technical Support, Operations, and Product to facilitate successful onboarding.
  • Establish clear customer expectations, implementation milestones, and success criteria.
  • Drive product adoption and ensure customers understand how to use DriveThruIQ effectively.
  • Identify deployment issues, adoption barriers, and risks to customer outcomes, coordinating resolution with the relevant teams.
3. Customer Retention & Relationship Management
  • Develop strong relationships with customer stakeholders across Operations, Technology, and Restaurant Development.
  • Maintain regular engagement with key accounts to understand satisfaction, challenges, and changing business priorities.
  • Monitor customer health, adoption, and engagement to identify potential retention risks.
  • Coordinate action plans to resolve issues and improve customer outcomes.
  • Escalate critical customer concerns and ensure clear ownership through to resolution.
4. Account Growth & Expansion
  • Work alongside Account Executives to identify opportunities for additional sites, brands, products, and markets.
  • Support account reviews by demonstrating product value and identifying opportunities for greater adoption.
  • Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities and communicate them to the relevant AE.
  • Support legacy-to-Vision / NextGen upgrade discussions through product demonstrations, customer education, and solution validation.
  • Help build customer business cases using operational outcomes and available performance data.
Commercial ownership remains with Sales and the Account Executives; CX enables customer value realization and identifies opportunities for growth.
5. Customer Advocacy & Value Realization
  • Establish measurable customer success criteria aligned to operational and commercial objectives.
  • Support customer reviews that demonstrate product adoption, performance improvements, and realized value.
  • Identify suitable customer references, testimonials, case studies, and peer-to-peer engagement opportunities.
  • Work with Marketing and Sales to turn successful deployments into advocacy and new-business opportunities.
6. Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Work closely with the Senior Director of Sales and Account Executives to align customer engagement with the regional GTM strategy.
  • Partner with global CX leadership, including Belinda Miksa, on strategic accounts, complex engagements, and critical customer relationships.
  • Coordinate with Product, Technical Support, and Operations to resolve issues affecting adoption and customer outcomes.
  • Maintain clear handover processes, account ownership, escalation pathways, and communication across teams.
  • Provide structured customer feedback to Product to inform roadmap priorities and improvements.
Key Performance Indicators
Performance will be measured against agreed targets, including:
  • Customer retention and renewal performance.
  • Product adoption and customer engagement.
  • Customer satisfaction and health.
  • Successful onboarding and solution validation.
  • Time to value following deployment.
  • Identification and progression of expansion opportunities with Sales.
  • Customer references, testimonials, and advocacy.
  • Timely resolution and escalation of customer issues.
Required Experience & Attributes
Customer Experience & Account Management
  • Experience in Customer Success, Customer Experience, Technical Account Management, or enterprise account management.
  • Proven ability to manage customer relationships throughout the post-sale lifecycle.
  • Experience supporting enterprise customers, ideally within multi-site or franchise-based businesses.
QSR & Technology Understanding
  • Experience in QSR, restaurant technology, SaaS, video analytics, POS, or adjacent technology markets is highly desirable.
  • Understanding of restaurant operations and the challenges facing multi-site operators.
  • Ability to explain technology in practical, commercially relevant terms.
Demonstration & Communication Skills
  • Confident presenting technology to operational, technical, and executive audiences.
  • Strong discovery, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to tailor demonstrations and customer engagement to business objectives.
Commercial Awareness
  • Understands how customer adoption, satisfaction, and value realization influence retention and expansion.
  • Able to identify growth opportunities and work collaboratively with Sales to progress them.
  • Comfortable using customer data, performance insights, and business cases to demonstrate value.
Ownership & Execution
  • Proactive, organized, and accountable for customer outcomes.
  • Able to coordinate cross-functional resources without losing ownership of customer actions.
  • Strong communication, documentation, and escalation discipline.
  • Comfortable working across a global organization and multiple time zones.
The Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is a commercially aware customer advocate who can bridge the gap between technology, restaurant operations, and business outcomes. They are confident demonstrating DriveThruIQ, supporting successful implementations, building customer relationships, and helping customers realize enough value to continue adopting and expanding the platform.
They understand that CX is not simply a reactive support function. It is a critical part of the growth model, ensuring customers achieve value, remain engaged, and become advocates for DTiQ.

Job Description:

Pluralsight is on a mission to shape the future of tech upskilling, and our brand is how the world meets that mission. We're looking for a multidisciplinary creative designer with outstanding conceptual thinking, exceptional design craft, and the ability to independently lead high-impact creative work.


As a Senior Graphic Designer at Pluralsight, you'll shape how our brand comes to life across campaigns, digital experiences, web, events, motion, and other marketing channels. You'll go beyond executing briefs to develop original concepts, establish creative direction, challenge conventional approaches, and deliver work that stands out in the market.


This is a hands-on, manager-caliber individual contributor role with significant creative ownership. You'll be trusted to lead complex initiatives, influence senior stakeholders, guide creative partners, and manage work from concept through delivery with minimal oversight. We're looking for someone who raises the standard of creative work while making the entire team more effective.


Everyone on our creative team is a maker. You'll remain deeply involved in concepting, designing, and producing work yourself while providing the creative leadership needed to keep projects moving and the team performing at its best.


What you'll do

  • Creative Direction and Execution
    • Independently concept, art direct, design, and execute distinctive creative across integrated campaigns, digital advertising, web, social, events, presentations, motion, and other brand experiences.
    • Translate business objectives and audience insights into compelling creative concepts that push beyond conventional B2B marketing approaches.
    • Own high-impact initiatives from strategy through final production, establishing visual direction while remaining actively involved in hands-on execution.
    • Develop cohesive campaign concepts and scalable design systems that balance originality, brand consistency, accessibility, and cross-channel effectiveness.
    • Help evolve Pluralsight's visual identity, identifying opportunities to strengthen differentiation and elevate creative quality.
  • Creative Leadership and Operational Ownership
    • Serve as a senior creative authority, independently making decisions and maintaining creative quality without requiring continuous oversight.
    • Lead creative projects through competing priorities, stakeholder feedback, approvals, and production, proactively resolving roadblocks and keeping work on track.
    • Provide art direction, critique, and hands-on guidance to designers, contractors, and agencies, improving both individual work and overall team output.
    • Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, improve collaboration, and expand creative capacity through scalable processes and emerging technologies, including AI.
  • Strategic Partnership and Influence
    • Confidently represent Creative in cross-functional and executive conversations, presenting recommendations and guiding stakeholders toward decisions.
    • Challenge prescriptive requests when appropriate, helping partners clarify business problems and develop stronger creative solutions.
    • Use audience insights, performance data, and experimentation to inform creative decisions and improve outcomes.

What you'll bring

  • Experience developing or evolving visual identity systems across multiple channels and customer experiences.
  • Strong understanding of responsive web design, usability, accessibility, and digital experience principles.
  • Experience working in B2B technology, SaaS, or other complex business environments.
  • Experience using AI-enabled tools and emerging creative technologies to improve exploration, production efficiency, or creative quality.

Requirements Qualifications

  • 8+ years of related experience (or equivalent combination of education and experience); or 6+ years of related experience with an advanced degree (Master’s/Doctorate).
  • An outstanding portfolio demonstrating original conceptual thinking, sophisticated visual execution, and multidisciplinary creative range.
  • Proven experience independently leading complex creative initiatives from concept through production, including establishing creative direction and making key decisions.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop distinctive integrated campaign concepts, not simply execute individual assets within established guidelines.
  • Advanced hands-on design capabilities, including expert command of typography, composition, visual storytelling, and design fundamentals.
  • Strong experience across brand and campaign design, with demonstrated versatility in digital, web, social, events, motion, or related disciplines.
  • Advanced proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Cloud.
  • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, present creative recommendations, navigate conflicting feedback, and achieve alignment.
  • Experience providing creative direction and improving the work of other designers or external creative partners.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage creative priorities, coordinate stakeholders, resolve challenges, and deliver high-quality work with minimal oversight.

Portfolio Expectations

Your portfolio should demonstrate more than polished design. We want to understand your creative thinking, ownership, and impact.


Be prepared to share examples of:

  • Original thinking: Distinctive concepts you developed and how you pushed beyond the initial brief or expected solution.
  • Independent leadership: Complex initiatives you led, including the creative decisions you personally owned.
  • Hands-on execution: Work you personally designed and produced, with clear attribution of your contributions.
  • Strategic influence: How you challenged assumptions, persuaded stakeholders, or navigated conflicting feedback to achieve a stronger outcome.
  • Creative impact: How your work improved business results, strengthened a brand, or elevated the output of other creative partners.

Portfolio quality, originality, creative judgment, and demonstrated impact will be significant factors in our evaluation.

Why you'll love working here

  • We work in a blended environment that supports collaboration, flexibility, and connection across teams.
  • We are mission-driven, shaping the future of tech upskilling and delivering impact that matters.
  • We foster a culture of inclusion and belonging, where everyone can contribute and thrive.
  • We are always learning, creating an environment where you can take on new challenges, expand your skills, and grow with purpose.
  • Benefits include competitive compensation, bonus eligibility, comprehensive medical coverage, unlimited PTO, wellness reimbursement, professional development funds, and more.

About us

Pluralsight provides the only learning platform dedicated to accelerating the technology skills and capabilities of today's tech workforce. Thousands of companies, government organizations and individuals around the world rely on Pluralsight to support critical technology skill development in areas that are crucial to innovation including artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity, software development, and machine learning. We offer highly curated content developed by vetted technology experts, industry leading skill assessments, and hands on, immersive learning experiences designed to help individuals skill-up faster.

Bring yourself. Pluralsight is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, or veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with EEOC guidelines and local laws.

If you need an accommodation to apply, interview, or perform essential job functions, please email . Learn more about our commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging in our DEIB Report.


Pay transparency

The annual US base salary range for this role is $91,200.00 - $120,000.00. Actual compensation will depend on location, skills, experience, and other factors. Additional benefits and bonuses may apply.


Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis

Please be aware of recruiting scams. We'll only contact you from an @pluralsight.com email or verified channels. We never ask for sensitive personal info or payments as part of the hiring process. All openings are posted on our Careers page.


AI use

Pluralsight uses AI-assisted features and separate automated technology to support parts of our recruiting process — for example, to help source candidates and draft job postings/descriptions, and to help flag potentially fraudulent or bot-generated applications for review. jobs.description:
Job Description:

Saybrook University, a private non-profit graduate institution, is widely recognized for its foundational contributions to humanistic psychology. Established to explore the full range of human experience, the university promotes personal transformation, social justice, and community well-being. Core faculty are central to Saybrook’s mission of educating leaders committed to building a more just, sustainable world.


The Department of Humanistic Clinical Psychology (HCP) offers a PhD program grounded in the scholar-practitioner model. The curriculum emphasizes strengths-based, holistic approaches rooted in the humanistic tradition. Delivered in a hybrid format, the program begins each semester with a week-long in-person residential session, followed by remote, online coursework.


Position Details:

  • Start Date: January 1, 2027 (1.0 FTE), or until filled
  • Location: Primarily remote, with a minimum required travel to California and less frequent rotational schedule to Washington State and Chicago, Illinois.

Position Summary: 

Core/Salaried Faculty Members at Saybrook University are dedicated to engaging in each of the following areas: Instruction and Curriculum Development, Student Support, Research and Scholarship and/or Professional Practice, University Learning Experiences (ULE), Masters/Project/Thesis/Essay/Dissertation Committees, and Departmental Support, including serving on university-wide committees, projects, and initiatives.


HCP is seeking a core/salaried faculty member, specifically with experience teaching and practicing psychological assessment.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities: 

I. Instruction & Curriculum Development 

  • Demonstrate command of subject matter in courses taught and administer assignments, exams, etc., that assess and continuously evaluate student progress, course effectiveness, and learning outcomes and adjust teaching strategies accordingly  
  • Demonstrate subject matter expertise for relevant industry career standards in the respective discipline  
  • Deliver high-quality online courses that foster critical thinking and strengthen clinical practice 
  • Classroom instruction includes lectures, demonstrations, discussions, or other appropriate modes of education delivery in a higher education via in-person and/or virtual formats 
  • Incorporate innovative teaching methods, technologies, learning styles, and program assessments that enhance andragogical learning and create a culture of inclusivity for a diverse student population  
  • Prepare course syllabi and plans in accordance with university and department requirements 
  • Provide timely and constructive feedback to students to support learning outcomes and encourage engagement 
  • Assess and revise course and program learning outcomes as needed 
  • As an SME, collaborate with department chair and leadership for the shared approval and retention of the design, development, and implementation of degree curriculum  
  • This includes developing new courses, updating current courses, and selecting appropriate textbooks and teaching aids as required 
  • Ensure course content and teaching methods are inclusive and reflective of diverse perspectives and backgrounds
  • Vetting, discernment, and shared approval of technology utilized to improve course delivery in a largely virtual environment 
  • Ensure course content and teaching methods are inclusive and reflective of diverse perspectives and backgrounds  
  • Create a safe and inclusive classroom environment 
  • Capacity to offer a variety of clinical psychology degree courses
  • Residential Learning Experiences: HCP faculty travel to California at the beginning of the fall, spring, and summer semesters for a week-long learning experience. Faculty present course introductions and clinical training workshops.
  • Faculty Retreat/Graduation: HCP faculty travel to California to participate in an annual faculty retreat and graduation ceremony.

II. Student Support  

  • Faculty Advising: Advise graduate students, maintaining a faculty advisee load according to the department's needs. Faculty advisors assist students with understanding pedagogy and course sequencing and support optimizing individual program plans to ensure student success and alignment with future career goals and interests.  
  • Faculty to Student Mentorship:Faculty support students in their professional development via mentorship of academic, curricular, research, and career pursuits 
  • Office Hours: Hold office hours to meet students’ needs 
  • Student Wellness:As a humanistic institution, Saybrook faculty are committed to ensuring student safety and Diversity Equity Inclusion Belonging (DEIB) across the university  
  • Student Resources: Appropriate referral to resources for academic, physical, mental, and emotional wellness as needed 
  • Student Research Supervision: Serve as chair or committee member on dissertations employing qualitative, quantitative, and/or mixed-method designs. May also supervise students' master's degree culminating project
     

III. Research, Scholarship & Professional Practice 

  • Saybrook University and its faculty are dedicated to excellence and innovation in research, scholarship, and/or professional practice in a variety of ways. Some examples include but are not limited to the following: 
  • Scholarly publications  
  • Speaking engagements (webinars, workshops, lectures, presentations, conferences, etc.) 
  • External board activities  
  • Funded projects, grants, and contracts 
  • Content Creation (new course/program development, revisions, web development, continuing education, etc.) 
  • Use of subject matter expertise (e.g., consultant, journal editor, reviewer for referred journal, peer reviewer of grants, speaker, service to government agencies, professional and industrial associations, educational institutions) 
  • Active engagement in clinical practice, supervision, consultation, or mentorship  
  • Creation/Development of new computer software, video or multimedia programs; Learning Management enhancements (e.g, interface options) 
  • Application of research and scholarship in the field, including new applications/methodologies developed and tested; new or enhanced systems and procedures demonstrated or evaluated for government agencies, professional and industrial associations, or educational institutions 
  • Other global impacts and creative accomplishment(s) 
  • Pursue continuous professional development to maintain subject matter expertise, such as attending conferences and engaging in scholarly activities. 

IV. Masters/Project/Thesis/Essay/Dissertation Committee Work 

  • Serve on masters, project, thesis, essay, and dissertation committees, providing critical input and guidance throughout each process 
  • Mentor students by guiding topic exploration, research question development, timeline management, writing expertise, IRB submission, and methodology assistance 
  • Dissertation Committee responsibilities as described in the Dissertations Policy and Procedures. Ensure that all dissertation activities comply with university guidelines and ethical standards for research. 

V. Departmental Support 

  • Participate in department meetings 
  • Involvement in prospective student selection processes  
  • Mentor faculty 
  • Collaborate with administrators (Deans, Associate Deans, Chairs, Associate Chairs, and Specialization Directors/Coordinators) and leadership around department planning 
  • Share in department practices, processes, and initiatives  

Service to the University and Community 

  • Faculty engage in university and community service in a variety of ways. Examples include but are not limited to the following: 
  • University Related Service  
  • University Committees - Contribute to departmental, college, and university committees and sub-committees (e.g., WSCUC) 
  • Governance (e.g., Faculty Senate) 
  • Accreditation  
  • IRB 
  • Search Committees 
  • Professional Service Outside of the University (e.g., Boards, committees, etc.) 
  • Community Service 
  • Engage in activities that promote the university's role in the community  
  • Participate in professional organizations and activities that contribute to the faculty’s respective field(s)  

Required Qualifications:  

  • Earned doctorate in clinical psychology from a regionally or APA-accredited institution
  • Licensure as a clinical psychologist
  • Experience teaching and practicing in psychological assessment
  • Strong commitment to the vision and goals of Saybrook University 
  • Commitment to excellence in teaching and research  
  • A distinguished record of scholarly achievements, including research publications and/or other contributions to the area of the program specialization. 
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate within an academic community and work in interdisciplinary settings  
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to foster positive relationships with students, faculty, staff, and external partners  
  • Promotes interdisciplinary working within and beyond the department 

Preferred Qualifications  

  • At least three (3) years of teaching experience at the graduate level
  • Licensed at the doctoral level for at least five (5) years
  • Experience teaching in an APA-accredited clinical training program
  • Governance involvement in the APA accreditation process
  • Experience with administering, scoring, writing, and/or teaching clinical assessments such as the WAIS, WISC, and MMPI-3
  • Demonstrated orientation toward innovation, experimentation, and change 
  • Experience in curriculum development and assessment  
  • Proficiency in online teaching platforms (e.g., Canvas)
  • Experience chairing dissertations
  • Background or experience teaching Existential Humanistic Psychology

Applications should include:

  • Cover Letter
  • Statement of Teaching Pedagogy & History
  • Statement of Research History
  • Value Statement (Potential candidates will review Saybrook University’s Mission and summarize how their individual values are related to the goals of the University)
  • Curriculum Vitae
  • Examples of Student Feedback (anonymous evaluation reports and/or letters of recommendation).

Compensation & Benefits

This opportunity is budgeted at $85,000.00 base compensation. Additional compensation factors may impact total compensation. To learn more about our competitive benefits and additional rewards, including generous paid time-off, medical and dental insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, retirement plan with employer contribution, multiple flexible spending accounts, tuition reimbursement, click the link below.

  6. Cross-reference maintenance tasks with FAA Parts 43, 121, 135, and 145 to ensure compliance and accurate process representation.

  3. Expertise with borescope engine inspection and interpretation of resulting imagery and reports.
  4. Proficiency in reading and interpreting maintenance manuals, IPCs, and approach plates.
  5. Thorough working knowledge of FAA Parts 43, 121, 135, and 145 regulations and real-world application.
  6. Exceptional written and verbal communication capabilities, with a strong attention to detail.
  7. Experience as a check airman or in training/mentoring roles within aviation maintenance settings is a plus.

Wer wir sind

cinify ist ein wachsendes HealthTech-Unternehmen aus Bochum. Mit unserer Software helfen wir Arztpraxen, medizinischen Einrichtungen und Gesundheitsunternehmen dabei, ihre Daten sinnvoll zu nutzen, Abläufe zu automatisieren und bessere Entscheidungen zu treffen.

Unsere Lösungen sind bereits erfolgreich im Gesundheitsmarkt im Einsatz. Jetzt wollen wir insbesondere im ambulanten Bereich weiter wachsen – und dafür suchen wir Dich.

Aufgaben

Du bist häufig der erste persönliche Kontakt zwischen cinify und potenziellen Kunden. Dein Ziel ist es, die richtigen Ansprechpartner zu erreichen, ihre Herausforderungen zu verstehen und qualifizierte Erstgespräche für unser Sales-Team zu vereinbaren oder auch selbst zu führen.

Dabei arbeitest Du nicht einfach eine Kontaktliste ab: Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns Zielgruppen, Gesprächsansätze und Kampagnen kontinuierlich weiter.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du identifizierst passende Arztpraxen und medizinische Einrichtungen.
  • Du sprichst Entscheider telefonisch, per E-Mail und über LinkedIn an.
  • Du findest heraus, welche Herausforderungen und Bedarfe potenzielle Kunden haben.
  • Du begeisterst Interessenten für cinify und vereinbarst qualifizierte Erstgespräche.
  • Du bereitest Gespräche gemeinsam mit unserem Sales-Team vor und begleitest die weitere Entwicklung der Verkaufschance.
  • Du dokumentierst Kontakte und nächste Schritte strukturiert in unserem CRM.
  • Du testest unterschiedliche Ansprachen und bringst eigene Ideen für unsere Neukundengewinnung ein.
  • Du hilfst uns dabei, einen erfolgreichen und skalierbaren Vertriebsprozess aufzubauen.

Dein Erfolg bemisst sich nicht daran, wie viele Anrufe Du machst, sondern daran, ob daraus gute Gespräche und echte Verkaufschancen entstehen.

Qualifikation

Das bringst Du mit:

  • Du kommunizierst gerne und hast keine Scheu davor, neue Menschen anzusprechen.
  • Du kannst gut zuhören, gezielt nachfragen und Interesse wecken.
  • Du arbeitest eigenständig, strukturiert und zuverlässig.
  • Rückschläge entmutigen Dich nicht – Du probierst neue Wege aus und bleibst dran.
  • Du interessierst Dich für digitale Produkte und möchtest verstehen, wie unsere Kunden arbeiten.
  • Du sprichst und schreibst sehr gutes Deutsch.

Erste Erfahrungen im Vertrieb, Kundenservice, Recruiting, Callcenter oder einer anderen kommunikationsstarken Tätigkeit sind hilfreich – aber kein Muss.

Besonders freuen wir uns über Erfahrung im Softwarevertrieb oder Gesundheitswesen. Viel wichtiger sind uns jedoch Deine Motivation, Dein Auftreten und Deine Bereitschaft, Dich weiterzuentwickeln.

Benefits

  • Eine zentrale Rolle beim weiteren Wachstum von cinify
  • Eine intensive Einarbeitung in unser Produkt, unsere Zielgruppen und modernen B2B-SaaS-Vertrieb

  • Kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen und ehrliches Feedback
  • Viel Freiheit, eigene Ideen auszuprobieren und Prozesse mitzugestalten

  • 100 % Remote-Arbeit innerhalb Deutschlands

  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit 20 % Arbeitgeberzuschuss

Du steigst nicht in einen fertigen Vertriebsapparat ein, in dem Du lediglich vorgegebene Skripte abarbeitest. Du lernst, wie Zielgruppen ausgewählt, Märkte erschlossen und aus ersten Kontakten langfristige Kundenbeziehungen entwickelt werden.

Copywriter, Traditional SEO & AI Search Visibility

Freelance Contract · Remote-first (Canada) · Works with the Head of Advisory

About podium iq

AI models now decide who gets recommended, considered and chosen. We measure how enterprise brands show up inside those answers, score them against the competitors that actually appear, and turn the finding into a content plan. Then we ship the content. Most of this category stops at the dashboard - we don’t, which is why our clients are financial institutions, global consumer technology brands, national regulating bodies, and major consulting firms.

The role

We’re building a roster of freelance writers we tap as enterprise work comes in.

Every brief you receive traces back to a specific opportunity podium found: a query where our client is invisible, a competitor winning a comparison, a topic with citation authority sitting unclaimed. You’ll know the target queries, the intent, the structure, and the sources before you start. What the brief can’t give you is the judgment, and that’s what we’re hiring.

You'll write for brands whose customers are making real decisions about money, technology, and the things they care about. Some briefs need nothing more than your craft. Others need you to go find the answer, interview a subject matter expert, or dive into secondary research until the content has something worth saying.


What you'll do

  • Write website copy, articles, FAQs, and supporting content from platform-derived briefs, built to be found in search and cited in AI answers.

  • Interrogate the brief before you write it. If the angle is wrong or the source material is thin, say so early.

  • Research properly. Read the client's material, understand their market, and get to the substance underneath the query.

  • Interview client subject matter experts when a piece needs primary insight, and occasionally walk a client through your work.

  • Work with our strategists on sprint timelines, turning quality around at pace.

  • Own your own quality control. Work arrives ready for client review.

What you bring

  • Five or more years writing professionally, with a portfolio that shows range and rigour.

  • Experience writing for SEO and GEO. You understand search intent, structure, internal linking, and source signals that get content cited in AI answers.

  • Command of what good actually is. You can explain why a piece works, and you can tell when a draft is competent and forgettable.

  • Research instinct. You go looking for the specific, the concrete, and the thing nobody else bothered to find out.

  • Comfort in front of a client. You can run an SME interview and get the good material out of someone who thinks they have nothing to say.

  • Speed with judgment intact.

  • A clear-eyed relationship with AI tooling. Use whatever helps you. What we are looking for underneath it is your own research, your own angle, and the taste to know when a draft has gone generic. That gap is the entire value of hiring a writer right now.

Where you specialize

We work across sectors and briefs will move you between them. Range across several is rare, depth in one is enough to get on the roster. We're actively looking for depth in:

  • Consumer financial services. Writing about money for real people, inside regulatory constraints.

  • Consumer brands and conversion. Writing that carries someone through a decision, from first curiosity to the moment they act, across retail, sport, and consumer products.

  • B2B and enterprise technology. Writing for buyers who know more than you do about their own problem.

  • Product marketing. Turning a feature into a reason to care.

The details

Freelance, project-based, open to writers anywhere in Canada. The rate is $70 to $90 per hour depending on experience, location, and specialization.

Roster writers are engaged per project as enterprise work comes in, so we don’t guarantee volume or ask for exclusivity. What we commit to a clear brief, a fair rate, fast decisions, and clarity about what’s coming. What we expect from those we onboard is accountability to the deadline and to the standard, without supervision. Sound like you? Here’s how to apply.

Send us:

  1. Two pieces of work you are proud of that also performed. Rankings, traffic, citations, conversions, or other business metrics.

  2. A short note on one of them: what you went and found out that made it better.

  3. An overview of the sectors your specialize in and number of years experience writing in those fields

jobs.description:
Director, Advisory Services: Financial Transformation - Revenue Cycle

*General travel requirements between 25-75% largely dependent on client engagement

About the Practice

Premier's Financial Transformation Advisory Practice reimagines the entire patient financial journey, from intake to invoice, helping health systems achieve sustainable margin improvement through an integrated, enterprise-wide approach. Rather than pursuing isolated fixes, our team works end-to-end across three interconnected pillars that drive lasting financial performance: Revenue Cycle, Managed Care, and Clinical Integrity. Our consultants combine trusted advisory relationships with advanced analytics, automation, and AI to help clients reduce friction, uncover hidden opportunities, strengthen accountability, and improve financial performance across the enterprise.

What You'll Be Doing

The Director serves as a senior leader within Premier's Financial Transformation Revenue Cycle Practice and is responsible for driving client outcomes, developing executive relationships, growing the business, and developing consulting talent. The Director acts as a trusted advisor to healthcare executives, providing strategic guidance on enterprise revenue cycle transformation, operational improvement, technology optimization, and financial performance enhancement.

The Director is accountable for leading complex client engagements, cultivating executive-level relationships, driving business development activities, overseeing engagement teams, and contributing to the growth and evolution of Premier's Revenue Cycle Practice. This role provides executive oversight for projects of all sizes and durations and maintains accountability for engagement quality, financial performance, client satisfaction, and achievement of measurable client outcomes.

The Director serves as a trusted advisor to CFOs, Chief Revenue Officers, Chief Operating Officers, Chief Information Officers, and other executive leaders, helping clients develop and execute strategic plans that improve operational performance, strengthen financial outcomes, and create sustainable organizational change.

In addition to client delivery responsibilities, the Director plays a significant role in business development, practice development, thought leadership, and talent development activities. The Director mentors Managers, Senior Consultants and Consultants, contributes to the development of innovative solutions and methodologies, and helps drive growth across the Revenue Cycle service line. This position collaborates with and develops strong client relationships across all levels of healthcare organizations, including executive leadership, revenue cycle operations, finance, clinical leadership, and technology teams, to achieve transformational results.

Core Expectations

  • Maintain utilization targets for client billable projects.
  • Create value through executive-level client relationship management, solution development, and implementation leadership.
  • Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to healthcare executives.
  • Develop and mentor future consulting leaders while fostering a collaborative and high-performing team environment.
  • Drive business growth through active participation in sales pursuits, account expansion activities, and new client development.
  • Create value for the Revenue Cycle Practice through thought leadership, innovation, methodology development, and practice enhancement initiatives.
  • Contribute to Premier's market presence through industry engagement, speaking opportunities, publications, and client-facing thought leadership.

Role-Specific Expectations

Directors within the Revenue Cycle Practice possess extensive expertise across the end-to-end revenue cycle, including patient access, revenue integrity, charge capture, coding, clinical documentation improvement, denials management, billing operations, collections, reimbursement optimization, and revenue cycle technology.

Additional expectations include:

  • Serve as an executive advisor to healthcare leadership teams on revenue cycle strategy, transformation, benchmarking, operational excellence, and financial improvement opportunities.
  • Lead enterprise-wide revenue cycle transformation initiatives that improve financial performance, operational efficiency, and patient experience.
  • Drive development and implementation of revenue enhancement, cash acceleration, denial reduction, and cost optimization strategies.
  • Build and maintain strong executive relationships with client stakeholders, serving as a trusted and referenceable advisor.
  • Lead strategic discussions regarding operating model design, organizational structure, technology optimization, governance, and performance management.
  • Apply advanced analytics, benchmarking, automation, and industry best practices to identify and quantify improvement opportunities.
  • Develop and enhance revenue cycle solutions, methodologies, intellectual property, and market offerings.
  • Sponsor implementation efforts and support achievement of measurable client outcomes.
  • Lead executive steering committees and facilitate consensus among clinical, operational, financial, and technology stakeholders.
  • Champion innovation and adoption of emerging technologies, including automation, artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and digital revenue cycle capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

Responsibility #1 – Client Delivery & Executive Leadership (50%)

  • Provide executive leadership and oversight for revenue cycle transformation engagements.
  • Serve as the primary executive relationship manager for assigned clients.
  • Lead executive-level discussions regarding organizational performance, strategic priorities, and transformation roadmaps.
  • Guide engagement teams in developing actionable recommendations and implementation plans that address client objectives.
  • Oversee complex operational, financial, technology, and performance analyses and ensure quality of engagement deliverables.
  • Facilitate executive steering committees, leadership workshops, and board-level presentations.
  • Manage engagement economics, profitability, scope, risk mitigation, and client satisfaction.
  • Ensure successful implementation and achievement of targeted financial and operational outcomes.
  • Sponsor large-scale transformation initiatives and support realization of sustainable improvement.
  • Identify opportunities for account growth and expanded client partnerships.
  • Direct and mentor Managers, Consultants, and Analysts assigned to engagements.
  • Serve as executive sponsor for key client relationships and strategic initiatives.

Responsibility #2 – Business Development & Account Growth (20%)

  • Develop, cultivate, and expand executive client relationships that generate additional revenue opportunities.
  • Lead sales pursuits, proposal development, statements of work, oral presentations, negotiations, and contracting activities.
  • Partner with practice leadership to achieve annual growth and revenue objectives.
  • Identify and qualify opportunities within existing and prospective client organizations.
  • Develop strategic account plans and expansion strategies for key client relationships.
  • Serve as an executive sponsor for strategic client accounts and growth initiatives.
  • Collaborate with Premier commercial and account management teams to identify and pursue market opportunities.
  • Actively generate new business through industry relationships, networking, conferences, and executive introductions.
  • Contribute to annual pipeline development, forecasting, and growth planning activities.
  • Support cross-selling opportunities across Premier service lines and solutions.

Responsibility #3 – Practice Development & Thought Leadership (15%)

  • Lead development and enhancement of revenue cycle methodologies, frameworks, intellectual property, and solution offerings.
  • Contribute to thought leadership activities, including conference presentations, webinars, publications, benchmark studies, and market-facing content.
  • Identify emerging healthcare and revenue cycle trends and translate those insights into innovative service offerings.
  • Collaborate with practice leadership to establish strategic priorities, market positioning, and service line growth plans.
  • Promote adoption of analytics, automation, AI, and technology-enabled solutions throughout client engagements.
  • Participate in strategic planning efforts supporting overall Advisory Services growth.
  • Help define and standardize leading practices for revenue cycle transformation engagements.
  • Collaborate with leadership to develop new offerings that address market demand and client needs.

Responsibility #4 – Talent Development & People Leadership (10%)

  • Mentor, coach, and develop Managers, Consultants, and Analysts across the practice.
  • Participate in recruiting, interviewing, hiring, onboarding, and retention activities.
  • Support succession planning and leadership development initiatives.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous learning.
  • Lead staffing and resource planning discussions across multiple engagements.
  • Provide ongoing performance coaching and career development guidance.
  • Identify high-potential talent and support advancement within the organization.
  • Promote employee engagement and professional development across the Revenue Cycle service line.

Responsibility #5 – Professional Development & Training (5%)

  • Complete all required training requirements annually.
  • Lead internal educational sessions and knowledge-sharing activities.
  • Support development of training materials and best practices within areas of expertise.
  • Stay current with industry trends, revenue cycle technologies, EMR platforms, regulatory developments, and emerging best practices.
  • Promote continuous learning and knowledge sharing throughout the Advisory Practice.

​Required Qualifications

Work Experience:

Years of Applicable Experience - 7 or more years

Education:

Bachelors (Required)

Work Experience

  • 10+ years of applicable healthcare experience.
  • 7+ years of experience leading revenue cycle operations, healthcare consulting engagements, or transformation initiatives.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex healthcare performance improvement programs.
  • Demonstrated experience influencing senior executives and leading large-scale transformational initiatives.

Education

  • Bachelor's Degree (Required)

Preferred Qualifications

Skills

  • Executive-level communication and presentation capabilities.
  • Ability to influence and advise C-suite and senior healthcare leaders.
  • Strong business development, relationship management, and consultative selling skills.
  • Expertise in revenue cycle operations, performance improvement, and financial transformation.
  • Ability to lead large, complex client engagements and multidisciplinary teams.
  • Experience developing innovative solutions and practice methodologies.
  • Proven people leadership and talent development capabilities.
  • Advanced analytical, strategic problem-solving, and financial management skills.
  • Ability to build trusted executive relationships and serve as a strategic advisor.

Experience

  • Revenue cycle leadership experience across acute care, ambulatory, physician enterprise, and integrated health systems.
  • Healthcare consulting experience focused on revenue cycle, financial transformation, operational improvement, or technology optimization.
  • Experience leading Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner, Meditech, or other revenue cycle technology transformation initiatives.
  • Track record of delivering measurable improvements in cash flow, denial reduction, revenue capture, productivity, and operating margins.
  • Proven success developing new business and expanding executive client relationships.
  • Experience leading enterprise-wide revenue cycle transformation programs involving operational, technology, and organizational change.

Education & Certifications

  • Master's Degree (MBA, MHA, MPH, or related field preferred).
  • HFMA, Lean Six Sigma, PMP, Epic Certification, CHFP, CRCR, or other relevant professional certifications preferred.

Additional Job Requirements:

  • Remain in a stationary position for prolonged periods of time

  • Be adaptive and change priorities quickly; meet deadlines

  • Attention to detail

  • Operate computer programs and software

  • Ability to communicate effectively with audiences in person and in electronic formats.

  • Day-to-day contact with others (co-workers and/or the public)

  • Making independent decisions

  • Ability to work in a collaborative business environment in close quarters with peers and varying interruptions

jobs.description:
Basic Function

Senior Account & Relationship Manager are subject matter experts when it comes to our products and the business processes which they facilitate. The Senior Account & Relationship Manager works with a broad cross-section of our pharmacy productivity customers to strengthen adoption; identify opportunities to expand the footprint and help ensure the renewal of our products. Our Senior Account & Relationship Manager work strategically with their customer base, to understand their business objectives, determine the best approach for leveraging Wolters Kluwer capabilities, and provide recommendations on how to proceed. Senior Account & Relationship Manager are strong contributors to this team of competitive and experienced professionals focused on customer satisfaction, customer retention, and our customer's Return on Investment (ROI)

Essential Duties and responsibilities

  • Proactively identify and prioritize pharmacy productivity accounts to focus efforts within a defined territory as based on perceived risk, potential growth, strategic value, and renewal timeframe.

  • Closely monitor adoption rates of assigned accounts; provide keen insight into exactly how customers are using our service, and help them to improve their ROI on the application.

  • Work closely with marketing and support and training to leverage best approach to efficiently and effectively communicate with customer base

  • Develop a complete understanding of Wolters Kluwer pharmacy productivity products and working knowledge of complementary products and services

  • Gather and create best practices for implementing and using our products to be disseminated to customers through content, conversations and presentations.

  • Act as liaison between product management and the customer to be an expert on the product, understand the roadmap and escalate critical product issues.

  • Facilitate transitions following new implementations or re-implementation.

  • Maintain up to date information in our Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system for assigned customer base.

  • Work collaboratively with Sales team who are responsible for driving revenue opportunities across a diverse account base through uncovering new business opportunities within the territory.

  • Maintain reference information on pharmacy productivity accounts

  • Take ownership of identified Red Accounts for assigned pharmacy productivity client base and ensures that action steps are completed and Red account status resolved.

  • Research and lockdown renewals that include a price increase and negotiate in the renewal process.

  • Be available to assist Implementation teams on issues that arise during implementation of our Standard accounts.

Other Duties

Performs other duties as assigned by supervisor.

  • High School diploma required or equivalent

  • BA/BS preferred

Minimum of 4 year's experience in a customer facing position that required a mix of proactive and reactive account management or interaction.

jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewAt Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department Overview

On any given day, every moment matters to someone, somewhere. And every moment, Motorola Solutions’ innovations, products and services play essential roles in people’s lives. We help firefighters see around buildings and police officers see around street corners. We keep utility workers connected and visible to each other with real-time voice and data communication across the smart grid. And we provide the situational awareness first responders need when a moment brings catastrophe. We help people be their best in their moments that matter when everyone around them is at their worst.


Guardian is a call taking & dispatching platform used by emergency service operators across the UK & Europe. We help 999 or 112 operators answer calls from the public and dispatch out nearby responders, enabling the right response when every second counts, and ultimately helping our customers save lives.


As our solution has grown from a small start-up to one of the leading offerings for Fire & Police agencies, our customers now trust us to solve more of their problems. The Guardian team is distributed across the UK. We currently have around 150 employees. We have a relaxed but hard working environment where jeans and t-shirts are the norm and good ideas and debate are encouraged. Our daily work is remote, with workflows managed via Google Chat & collaborative documents in G-Suite. However, you’ll also have the opportunity to join us in person at work & social events or our annual all-hands in top European cities like Prague, Barcelona, and Krakow.


Job Description

Back End Developer (Temporary) - remote with occasional travel to Motorola offices.

The role of the Software Engineer is to work as part of an agile delivery team to design and develop the software solutions. You will work closely with the other members of the development team, then Product Manager, and the Software Test Engineers.

You'll be developing mission critical or supporting software to a high standard, including design, development, technical documentation, and testing.

Our backend tech stack is C#.NET.


Basic Requirements

We are looking for someone who

  • Has experience as a Software Developer or significant experience as a Junior Software Developer

  • Has experience building backend systems in C# .NET,

  • Is passionate about writing high-quality code

  • Can demonstrate good technical ability

  • Understands modern software development practices and principles, such as SOLID

  • Understands modern development workflows, including agile process, Git repositories, pull requests

​

Core Competencies:

  • 3+ years of hands-on back end software development using C# .NET.

  • Solid understanding of OOP, design patterns and software engineering principles.

The Senior Technical Services Manager is responsible for leading the fleet's shared technical services capability, maintaining a fleet-wide perspective on vessel maintenance, asset performance, and technical support while building long-term future readiness. Reporting to the Director of Technical Operations, the role leads the specialist team and allocates its support to Technical Superintendents and Asset Management teams, adjusting priorities against competing fleet demands. The role develops and maintains fleet technical standards and drives technical readiness across the fleet by balancing immediate operational needs with long-term reliability, maintainability and lifecycle objectives.

  • Lead the Technical Services Team and allocate the shared specialist bench: aligns priorities, manages performance, and schedules specialists across machinery, electrical, navigation, hospital, accommodation, deck, and other assigned systems, resolving competing demands against fleet priorities across AMPs, dry dockings, defect resolution, and major technical work.
  • During AMPs and vessel work, Technical Services specialists work under the direction of the Technical Superintendent responsible for the vessel.
  • Keep specialists closely engaged with vessel engineering, electrical, and biomedical teams to surface technical pain points early.
  • Coordinate the team's specialist support for complex, cross-disciplinary, or recurring vessel issues, engaging third-party vendors and driving structured defect reporting where specialist input is needed, while the responsible Technical Superintendent owns resolution for the vessel.
  • Leads the implementation and continuous improvement of engineering practices and maintenance strategy while ensuring the quality and content of the planned maintenance system, in coordination with the Fleet Technical Manager.
  • Collaborate across the disciplines and teams for engineering review and acceptance recommendations on complex repairs, modifications, upgrades and technical solutions.
