jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

LMG Staffing Solutions is conducting a confidential search on behalf of a fast-growing, fully remote marketing agency that helps funded B2B SaaS and technology companies win visibility in traditional and AI-powered search. The company has nearly doubled revenue over the past year and is building its first-ever sales development function to keep pace with a growing stream of inbound demand. This is a newly created role reporting directly to the Founder, sitting outside the delivery-focused teams (content, strategy, and link building).

Position Summary

The Sales Development Representative (SDR) will be the first point of contact for a steady stream of inbound, outbound (ABM), and reactivation leads, and will play a key role in building the company’s outbound systems from the ground up. This is not a generic dialer role — the ideal candidate has real experience selling into B2B SaaS or funded tech startups, can hold a credible first conversation with senior marketing and growth buyers, and is motivated to grow into a more senior sales role as the function scales. The role starts part-time (~20 hours/week), with a 90-day review for a move to full-time based on performance and lead volume.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

Lead Response & Qualification

  • Respond same-day, ideally within the hour, to every inbound, outbound (ABM), and reactivation handoff — across email, LinkedIn, and phone/text
  • Qualify every lead against ICP criteria, protecting the founder’s calendar from below-budget or bad-fit prospects
  • Book qualified discovery calls — turning a reply into a booked next step is the core measure of the role

Multi-Channel Outbound & Prospecting

  • Run second-channel follow-up (call, text, LinkedIn) wherever email goes quiet on handoffs from inbound and ABM
  • Self-source prospecting against the company’s ICP during downtime between handoffs — LinkedIn outreach and targeted email to build pipeline beyond inbound and ABM
  • Support the development and execution of high-value, niche outbound campaigns (e.g., targeted email and direct mail to a curated list of key accounts) in partnership with the founder

CRM & Sales Systems

  • Keep the CRM clean and current — every touch, stage move, and next action logged as you go
  • Help select, configure, and maintain outreach tooling as the company builds out its sales stack; the team is open to your recommendations on platforms

Coaching & Growth

  • Shadow the founder’s calls and playbook early on, then operate independently as you prove it out
  • Build toward a more senior sales role as the function and lead volume scale

Qualifications

  • B2B SaaS or sales-development experience, ideally selling to funded tech startups — prioritized over specific SEO or digital-marketing expertise
  • Able to hold a credible first conversation with marketing, growth, or founder-level buyers
  • Exposure to the SEO/AEO or digital-marketing space is a plus, but not required
  • Organized and responsive across multiple channels — phone, LinkedIn, email, and CRM
  • Coachable and fast-learning, comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy in a lean, remote-first environment
  • Based in the United States; Eastern or Central time zone preferred to support overlap with a globally distributed team and West Coast clients (soft preference)

Preferred Skills

  • Multi-Channel Outbound Prospecting
  • Lead Qualification (ICP-Based)
  • B2B SaaS / Tech Startup Sales Experience
  • CRM Management & Pipeline Hygiene
  • Sales Outreach Tool Selection & Setup (e.g., Apollo or similar)
  • Relationship Building & Written Communication
  • Cold Email & Direct Mail Campaign Development

What Success Looks Like

  • Response speed (non-negotiable): same-day, within-the-hour response on every handoff, no exceptions
  • Booked calls: 15–20 qualified discovery calls booked per month, roughly one per day, across handoff response and self-sourced outreach
  • The founder stops being the bottleneck on responding to his own pipeline

Benefits

Uncapped commission — 5% on every deal you personally book that closes, and with 2–6 week sales cycles, commission can quickly exceed the base pay

Fast path to full-time — 90-day review with an updated, higher base if it's working well for both sides

Fully remote, flexible part-time schedule (~20 hrs/week)

Direct mentorship from the founder — shadow live sales calls and the playbook early on

Ground-floor ownership — help build the company's first-ever outbound sales systems and tooling from scratch

High-growth environment — the company nearly doubled revenue this year with a goal to triple, meaning real room to grow into a more senior sales role

**PLEASE SUBMIT YOUR CV IN ENGLISH**

Location: Remote – Latin America
Work Arrangement: Fully Remote
Employment Type: Full-Time
Compensation:$2,000–$3,000 USD/month
English Proficiency:C2 / Near-Native English Required
Schedule:9:00 AM–5:00 PM U.S. Eastern Time availability required
Industry: Investment Management / Alternative Investments

About the Company

Our client is a fast-growing U.S.-based investment management firm building institutional-quality alternative investment solutions for investors, financial advisory firms, and multi-family offices.

The company operates a sophisticated investment platform that includes its own investment funds as well as customized fund-of-funds solutions for financial partners. With assets under management growing rapidly and additional investment products in development, the firm is expanding its operational infrastructure to support its next stage of growth.

The organization combines the innovation and agility of a technology-driven company with the rigor, controls, and sophistication of institutional investment management.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Fund Operations Manager to take hands-on ownership of the operational processes that keep a growing investment fund platform running accurately and efficiently.

This is a specialized fund operations role with responsibility across the monthly NAV cycle, fund accounting, investor transactions, KYC/AML, capital activity, investor reporting, management-company accounting, fund launches, and external provider coordination.

You will work closely with the Head of Operations and serve as a trusted operational partner capable of independently managing critical fund processes from beginning to end.

This is not a traditional back-office role. You will have significant ownership, direct exposure to investors and leadership, and the opportunity to improve and automate fund operations as the platform scales.

What You'll Do

NAV & Fund Accounting

  • Own the monthly NAV process and drive the close through final review and sign-off.

  • Coordinate month-end activities with fund administrators and other external providers.

  • Prepare and review monthly NAVs, identifying and resolving discrepancies before leadership review.

  • Reconcile positions and cash across internal calculations, shadow records, and official administrator records.

  • Manage outstanding manager NAVs and help maintain an efficient and timely close process.

  • Maintain accurate fund performance records, including returns, positions, and expenses.

  • Ensure fund accounting records remain complete, accurate, and audit-ready.

Investor Operations

  • Process investor subscriptions, redemptions, and transfers accurately and on time.

  • Own KYC/AML onboarding processes and maintain an accurate investor register.

  • Coordinate capital calls, distributions, fee calculations, payments, and wire approvals.

  • Serve as a front-line point of contact for investors, handling operational questions with accuracy, professionalism, and discretion.

  • Coordinate directly with external administrators, managers, and service providers to resolve investor-related requests.

Investor Reporting

  • Produce quarterly fact sheets and investor performance reporting using fund control-book data.

  • Support quarterly fund-of-funds reporting and commentary processes.

  • Maintain complete and organized shadow and official NAV records.

  • Identify opportunities to automate recurring reporting and data processes.

Management Company Accounting & Financial Operations

  • Manage the management company's books, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, bookkeeping, and month-end close.

  • Prepare recurring management financial reporting, including KPIs, management-fee tracking, and expense reporting.

  • Coordinate invoices, payments, expense management, and financial records.

  • Help bring recurring bookkeeping and reporting processes in-house while improving and automating them wherever possible.

Fund Formation & Launch

  • Support the operational setup and launch of new funds.

  • Coordinate account openings, documentation, and required registrations.

  • Help establish the operational infrastructure for new funds and feeder structures.

  • Ensure new fund launches are executed accurately without disrupting existing fund operations.

Providers, Controls & Operational Infrastructure

  • Manage day-to-day coordination with fund administrators, transfer agents, prime brokers, and banks.

  • Maintain strong controls around operating accounts, fund accounts, and wire approvals.

  • Document fund operations procedures and build scalable operational playbooks.

  • Create reliable processes that provide operational continuity and reduce dependency on any single team member.

  • Continuously identify opportunities to improve, streamline, and automate fund operations.

Required Qualifications

  • C2 / Near-native English proficiency, written and spoken.

  • 5+ years of hands-on fund operations experience within a fund administrator, hedge fund, private markets manager, fund-of-funds, asset manager, or similar investment environment.

  • Strong hands-on experience managing the NAV cycle, investor transactions, and capital activity.

  • Strong fund accounting foundation, including NAV review, position and cash reconciliation, P&L, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow.

  • Ability to independently identify and resolve errors in monthly NAVs before final approval.

  • Hands-on experience with subscriptions, redemptions, transfers, KYC/AML, capital calls, distributions, and fee calculations.

  • Experience coordinating with fund administrators, transfer agents, prime brokers, and banks.

  • Hands-on accounting experience with accounts payable, accounts receivable, bookkeeping, month-end close, and financial reporting.

  • Experience communicating directly with investors or external financial partners.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and a strong controls mindset.

  • High level of ownership, judgment, discretion, and follow-through.

  • Ability to work independently and manage critical financial processes from beginning to end.

  • Availability during U.S. Eastern business hours (9:00 AM–5:00 PM ET).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience within alternative investments or asset management.

  • Fund-of-funds or multi-strategy investment experience.

  • Experience working with multiple funds simultaneously.

  • Experience with feeder funds, holding-company structures, or onshore/offshore investment structures.

  • Experience supporting new fund launches and fund formation.

  • Experience working directly with founders, investors, and external financial service providers.

  • Experience using AI and automation to improve reconciliation, reporting, or recurring fund operations processes.

Tools & Systems

Experience with every platform is not required, but candidates should be comfortable learning sophisticated financial and operational systems quickly.

Relevant tools may include:

  • Fund administration and NAV platforms

  • Fund performance tracking systems

  • Prime brokerage platforms

  • Accounting and expense-management systems

  • SharePoint

  • Google Workspace

  • Slack

  • Notion

  • Linear

  • Claude, Codex, and AI automation tools

What Success Looks Like

The ideal candidate combines deep fund operations expertise with exceptional precision and ownership.

You are someone who:

  • Owns the close: You manage the monthly NAV cycle end to end, proactively resolve issues, and keep the close on schedule.

  • Operates with precision: You reconcile before approving, identify discrepancies others may miss, and build controls that prevent errors.

  • Can be trusted with investor capital: You handle sensitive financial and investor information with exceptional judgment and discretion.

  • Takes complete ownership: Once a responsibility is handed to you, leadership can trust that it will be completed accurately and on time.

  • Improves the system: You continuously look for opportunities to streamline, document, and automate recurring fund operations.

Why Join Us

  • Competitive compensation paid in USD.

  • Fully remote opportunity.

  • Work directly with senior leadership at a growing U.S. investment management firm.

  • Significant ownership over critical fund operations.

  • Exposure to sophisticated alternative investment and fund-of-funds structures.

  • Opportunity to help build and scale the operational infrastructure behind a growing investment platform.

  • Technology-forward environment with opportunities to automate and improve traditional fund operations.

Important Notes

Please submit your CV in English.

Candidates should have direct, hands-on experience in fund operations and fund accounting. General business operations or accounting experience without meaningful exposure to investment fund operations will not be sufficient for this position.

This is a remote/telecommute position.

At STN, we don't just adapt to the digital future, we engineer it. Our mission is to help organizations thrive in a rapidly evolving technology landscape through strategic insight, cutting-edge solutions, and a security-first mindset. We provide end-to-end services spanning cloud consulting, AI infrastructure, and enterprise security, enabling secure, scalable, and future-ready transformation.

As trusted advisors, we align IT investments with business outcomes that drive performance and growth, starting with deep strategic engagement and delivering tailored solutions built for long-term impact.

Our approach is innovation-led and rooted in cybersecurity, with a focus on leveraging the right technologies to solve real-world challenges. We invest in our people and foster a culture of growth, inclusion, and purpose because we believe empowered teams build transformative technology.

Overview

The Technical Success Manager is responsible for the operational, technical, and lifecycle success of assigned managed-services customers. The position serves as a primary relationship and coordination point between the customer and STN’s Service Desk and Managed Services Operations, Engineering, Project Management Office, Sales, Procurement, Finance, and leadership teams.

The Technical Success Manager develops and maintains an informed understanding of each customer’s business, stakeholders, technology environment, managed-services agreement, support history, active initiatives, asset lifecycle, and upcoming contractual obligations. The role facilitates recurring customer meetings, monitors service performance and escalations, tracks commitments, coordinates ongoing initiatives, supports asset and technology lifecycle planning, and ensures that contract, licensing, warranty, and service renewals are identified and addressed in advance.

This is a non-commissioned role. The Technical Success Manager identifies customer needs and qualified improvement opportunities but transfers solution design, pricing, negotiation, forecasting, and closing responsibilities to the appropriate Sales, Solutions, or contract-management resources.

Key Responsibilities

Customer relationship and account knowledge

  • Serve as a primary operational point of contact for assigned managed-services customers.
  • Build relationships with customer executives, business leaders, technical contacts, department managers, and escalation stakeholders.
  • Understand each customer’s business operations, critical technology dependencies, supported locations, key vendors, communication preferences, and service expectations.
  • Maintain an accurate stakeholder map identifying decision-makers, technical contacts, executive sponsors, renewal owners, and escalation contacts.
  • Maintain awareness of customer sentiment, organizational change, operational risks, business priorities, and upcoming initiatives.
  • Represent the customer’s interests internally while maintaining contractual, technical, and operational boundaries.

Customer meeting management

  • Coordinate and attend weekly, monthly, quarterly, and other scheduled customer meetings based on account requirements.
  • Prepare agendas using ticket activity, service performance, project status, lifecycle items, renewals, open decisions, risks, and upcoming initiatives.
  • Facilitate meetings or support the designated meeting owner.
  • Document decisions, owners, due dates, risks, dependencies, and follow-up actions.
  • Distribute meeting notes and action summaries within the established service standard.
  • Track customer commitments through completion and escalate overdue or blocked actions.
  • Assist with monthly service reviews, quarterly business reviews, executive reviews, and technology-planning discussions.

Support ticket and service oversight

  • Review open tickets, aging tickets, escalations, recurring incidents, reopened tickets, and customer-impacting trends for assigned accounts.
  • Monitor high-priority and customer-sensitive issues to confirm ownership, communication cadence, and appropriate escalation.
  • Follow up on tickets and initiate with Managed Services Operations, who remain responsible for completing the work; keep informed and help move stalled tickets forward.
  • Help ensure customer-facing updates are timely, accurate, understandable, and aligned with confirmed technical information.
  • Identify patterns that may require root-cause analysis, problem management, technical remediation, training, lifecycle replacement, or project work.
  • Review relevant SLA performance, ticket volume, response trends, resolution trends, and backlog information.
  • Avoid bypassing established service ownership or directly assigning technical work outside approved processes.

Customer environment understanding

  • Develop a working account-management understanding of the customer’s environment, including:
  • STN Provided services and how they interact within their environment which may include:
    • Servers, cloud services, virtualization, storage, and business-critical applications.
    • Network, internet, wireless, firewall, remote-access, and connectivity services.
  • Cybersecurity, monitoring, logging, vulnerability, and compliance-related services.
  • Backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, and recovery objectives.
  • Locations, facilities, remote-work requirements, and key third-party dependencies.
  • Managed-services agreement, supported scope, service exclusions, and customer responsibilities.

Asset and technology lifecycle management

  • Maintain visibility into supported customer assets and technology platforms using the designated systems of record.
  • Track or validate purchase dates, deployment dates, warranties, leases, vendor support, end-of-sale, end-of-support, and end-of-life information.
  • Identify unsupported, aging, or capacity-constrained technology before it creates an operational emergency.
  • Coordinate with technical teams to validate lifecycle risks, replacement timing, dependencies, and recommended next steps.
  • Maintain a rolling 12, 18, or 24 month lifecycle forecast for assigned customers.
  • Bring upcoming lifecycle needs into customer service reviews, budgeting discussions, and QBRs.
  • Confirm that completed replacements, upgrades, and decommissions are reflected in asset and customer documentation.
  • Escalate material asset-data gaps and coordinate corrective action with the responsible team.

Contract, licensing, warranty, and renewal management
  • Maintain a consolidated renewal calendar for managed-services agreements, licensing, subscriptions, warranties, leases, connectivity, cloud, security, backup, and relevant third-party services.
  • Begin renewal preparation within the company’s required advance window.
  • Validate customer quantities, users, devices, locations, service tiers, usage, asset status, and current requirements.
  • Identify material differences between contracted quantities, deployed quantities, billed quantities, and customer expectations.
  • Coordinate with Sales, Procurement, Finance, Contract Administration, and technical teams to resolve discrepancies.
  • Prepare a renewal-readiness summary documenting expiration date, current services, quantities, expected changes, stakeholder contacts, known concerns, technical recommendations, required approvals, and target completion date.
  • Schedule or support customer renewal-planning discussions and track quotes, approvals, signatures, purchase orders, provisioning, and billing updates.
  • Escalate renewals that are delayed, incomplete, commercially at risk, or operationally critical.
  • Confirm completed renewals are reflected in Salesforce, NetSuite, the contract repository, billing, the STN One portal, and customer documentation.

Initiative and light project coordination

  • Maintain visibility into active customer projects, upgrades, remediations, onboarding activities, and operational initiatives.
  • Coordinate with PMO to understand schedules, milestones, dependencies, customer responsibilities, risks, and expected completion dates.
  • Communicate confirmed status information during customer meetings.
  • Track customer decisions, approvals, access requirements, scheduling needs, and other dependencies that may affect delivery.
  • Perform light coordination for small operational initiatives when a formal Project Manager is not assigned and when ownership is explicitly delegated.
  • Escalate scope, budget, resource, schedule, and delivery risks to the responsible Project Manager or operational leader.
  • Avoid making commitments regarding project scope, budget, resources, or completion dates without confirmation from the accountable owner.

Proactive improvement and Sales handoff

  • Identify potential improvements based on service trends, technical findings, lifecycle risks, contract changes, customer requests, business changes, and documented gaps.
  • Recognize potential needs involving security, lifecycle replacement, licensing, cloud, backup, disaster recovery, networking, compliance, training, or managed services.
  • Document the customer problem, business impact, urgency, known technical context, relevant stakeholders, timing, and required technical validation.
  • Create or initiate the opportunity record using the established Salesforce or portal process.
  • Conduct a structured handoff to Sales and participate in discovery when customer or account context is required.
  • Track whether the customer receives timely follow-up and maintain account-level visibility into opportunity status.
  • Do not present unapproved pricing, negotiate terms, promise discounts, or function as the closing salesperson.

Escalation management

  • Follow the company’s technical, service, executive, contractual, security, and sales escalation paths.
  • Confirm customer impact, urgency, current owner, communication expectations, and next-update time.
  • Ensure the appropriate leaders and technical resources are engaged.
  • Maintain a clear record of actions, decisions, owners, risks, and communications.
  • Support post-incident follow-up and lessons-learned activities when appropriate.
  • Identify escalations that indicate broader customer-health, service-scope, contract, or relationship risk. ​​​​​​​
Documentation, reporting, and internal coordination
  • Maintain an account-success plan for each assigned customer.
  • Keep stakeholder, environment, contract, lifecycle, renewal, initiative, risk, and escalation records current.
  • Conduct recurring internal account reviews with Service Delivery, Managed Services Operations, Engineering, PMO, Sales, Procurement, Finance, and leadership as appropriate.
  • Provide leadership with visibility into account health, upcoming renewals, lifecycle exposure, open commitments, escalations, and commercial handoffs.
  • Use the STN One portal, Atlassian products (Jira and Confluence), the ticketing system, Salesforce, NetSuite, monitoring tools, and other approved platforms according to defined processes.
  • Support customer onboarding, transitions, offboarding, and material environment changes, and validate that onboarding (G.9) and offboarding (G.11) duties are complete.
  • Identify possible service-scope misunderstandings or recurring out-of-scope requests and route them for review.

Experience & Qualifications

Required

  • Four or more years of experience in an MSP, IT service-delivery, technical account-management, customer success, or comparable customer-facing technical role.
  • At least two years managing customer relationships, escalations, recurring reviews, or an assigned account portfolio.
  • Operational working knowledge of networks, servers, cloud services, cybersecurity, monitoring, backup, and disaster recovery.
  • Experience reviewing support tickets, service metrics, customer escalations, and recurring issue trends.
  • Experience coordinating technical projects, upgrades, remediation activities, or customer initiatives.
  • Experience using a PSA, CRM, ticketing system, documentation platform, project system, asset platform, or monitoring portal.
  • Ability to interpret service descriptions, contract dates, licensing quantities, warranties, and renewal requirements.
  • Strong written communication, meeting facilitation, organization, documentation, and follow-through skills.
  • Ability to communicate credibly with customer executives, business contacts, and technical teams.
  • Sound judgment regarding when to involve Service Delivery, Engineering, Security, PMO, Sales, Finance, Procurement, Legal, or leadership.

Preferred

  • Direct Managed Service Provider employment experience.
  • Experience leading monthly service reviews, QBRs, executive reviews, or technology-planning meetings.
  • Experience with contract renewals, software licensing, hardware warranties, leases, or vendor services.
  • Experience developing asset or technology lifecycle plans.
  • Experience with Atlassian Jira and Confluence, a customer portal, PSA, CRM, RMM or monitoring tools, and IT documentation platforms.
  • ITIL 4 Foundation, Microsoft Fundamentals, CompTIA, CAPM, Project+, or similar relevant certification.
  • Experience working with regulated or compliance-sensitive customers.

Physical and work requirements

  • Regular use of video conferencing, collaboration tools, ticketing systems, dashboards, and customer portals.
  • Ability to participate in meetings across supported customer time zones.
  • Periodic customer, company, or vendor travel as required by account needs.
  • Occasional participation in urgent customer escalations outside the normal meeting schedule.
  • Reasonable accommodations will be considered in accordance with applicable law and company policy.

Benefits

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and reference verification. All applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

jobs.excerpt: TEHORA est présentement à la recherche d’un(e) responsable technique Solaris senior - niveau 3 afin de contribuer au développement et à l’exploitation de son centre de services Unix/Solaris.
jobs.description:
TEHORA est présentement à la recherche d’un(e) responsable technique Solaris senior - niveau 3 afin de contribuer au développement et à l’exploitation de son centre de services Unix/Solaris. La personne retenue prendra en charge les incidents complexes, encadrera les changements à haut risque et participera à la conception des stratégies de migration, de modernisation et de relève pour des environnements critiques.

Sans être exhaustifs, voici les services et livrables que devra fournir la personne retenue :

  • Agir à titre de référence technique de niveau 3 pour les environnements Oracle Solaris et SPARC;
  • Analyser et résoudre les incidents majeurs ou complexes liés au démarrage, à OpenBoot PROM, au boot-device, aux zones, aux LDOM, à ZFS, à UFS, au réseau et au stockage;
  • Définir, réviser et approuver les normes techniques, procédures d’exploitation, plans de changement, plans de retour arrière et critères de validation;
  • Concevoir et encadrer des migrations Solaris 10 vers Solaris 11, UFS vers ZFS, SPARC T-Series ainsi que des migrations de stockage SAN;
  • Évaluer les risques, dépendances applicatives, fenêtres d’intervention et mécanismes de retour arrière avant les changements critiques;
  • Diriger les analyses de causes profondes et produire les recommandations faisant suite aux incidents majeurs;
  • Concevoir ou réviser les plans de continuité, de redondance et de reprise informatique, incluant les RTO, RPO et scénarios de tests;
  • Coordonner les escalades techniques auprès d’Oracle, d’IBM et des autres fournisseurs lorsque requis;
  • Encadrer les administrateurs Solaris de niveau 2, assurer le mentorat et contribuer au transfert de connaissances;
  • Participer à une rotation d’astreinte planifiée et aux interventions critiques hors des heures normales lorsque requis.

Requirements

  • Détenir un BAC ou un DEC en informatique, ou une formation équivalente, combiné à une expérience pertinente importante;
  • Posséder au moins 10 années d’expérience en technologies de l’information, dont au moins 8 années en administration et architecture Solaris;
  • Maîtriser Solaris 10 et Solaris 11, les serveurs SPARC, LDOM, CDOM, Solaris Zones, UFS, ZFS et OpenBoot PROM;
  • Posséder une expérience avancée des environnements SAN et Fibre Channel : HBA, zoning, LUN, multipathing, performance et diagnostic;
  • Connaître IBM SVC, IBM Storwize, V5000 ou V7000 constitue un atout important;
  • Posséder une expérience en migration, haute disponibilité, sauvegarde, restauration et reprise après sinistre;
  • Avoir de bonnes connaissances de Linux, Oracle, VMware, TCP/IP, DNS, NTP, VLAN et outils de surveillance;
  • Une certification Oracle Solaris 11 ou une certification équivalente constitue un atout important;
  • Très bonne maîtrise du français parlé et écrit; anglais technique fonctionnel;
  • Leadership technique, calme en situation critique, jugement, autonomie et excellente capacité de documentation.

Benefits

  • Télétravail et flexibilité selon les mandats;
  • Horaires flexibles et planification structurée des périodes d’astreinte;
  • Projets technologiques stimulants dans des environnements critiques et institutionnels;
  • Environnement collaboratif et multidisciplinaire;
  • Possibilité de contribuer au développement d’une nouvelle pratique spécialisée Unix/Solaris chez TEHORA.

SALAIRE

La rémunération sera déterminée selon l’expérience, le profil et le statut d’engagement retenu.

LIEU DE TRAVAIL

Québec - Télétravail principalement, avec présence ponctuelle chez les clients au Québec. Participation à une rotation d’astreinte et à certaines interventions planifiées le soir ou la fin de semaine.

POURQUOI SE JOINDRE À TEHORA ?

TEHORA est une firme québécoise multidisciplinaire reconnue pour l’excellence de ses services professionnels, de nature technique et de gestion de projets à l’échelle nationale et internationale. Notre mission est d’accompagner nos clients dans la concrétisation de leurs projets par l’excellence de notre savoir-faire et de notre créativité.

Depuis sa création en 2017, notre équipe de professionnels connaît une croissance exponentielle en répondant aux besoins importants en gestion de projets multidisciplinaires, dans le domaine des transports, du génie civil, du TI et plus.

Nos collaborateurs travaillent sur des mandats aussi bien à l’interne que chez des clients d’envergure.

TEHORA se distingue par sa culture d’entreprise, axée sur le bonheur de ses employés et la diversité.

Chez TEHORA, chaque collaborateur est un membre important de l’équipe qui contribue à notre succès collectif. Nos membres ont la flexibilité requise pour avoir un équilibre entre le travail et leur vie privée, tout en menant une carrière enrichissante.

Nous offrons un environnement de travail motivant. La diversité des projets, la grande autonomie et l’interaction directe avec les clients sont appréciées. Une telle proximité est possible en raison de notre structure organisationnelle horizontale, qui se traduit par des relations de confiance et une communication efficace entre notre équipe et les clients.

Actionstep is a pioneer in the development and sale of software-as-a-service (SaaS) products, specializing in the delivery of Legal Practice Management and Legal Accounting software. We are a fast-growing, dynamic business with a global customer base of more than 50,000 and a team of over 250 across the USA, Australia, UK, Canada, and New Zealand.

Actionstep is expanding its product portfolio and adding richer AI functionality across the platform to deepen customer value, accelerate cross-sell revenue, and introduce new add-on modules that increase competitive differentiation.

THE PURPOSE OF YOUR ROLE

The Strategic Finance Analyst is a core contributor to Actionstep’s Finance team. The role’s initial focus areas are core FP&A work, including forecasting and profitability analysis; gross margin and pricing analysis; and commission calculations across Sales, Partner, and Operations teams. You will report to the VP of Finance and work closely with the broader Finance and RevOps teams. As Actionstep’s needs evolve, the specific mix of responsibilities may shift, and you may take on additional or different analytical work over time.

ABOUT YOU

You are a strong financial analyst who thinks in numbers first, and you’re just as comfortable in the data and systems behind those numbers as you are in a spreadsheet. You build clean, reliable models and analysis, and you understand that the work behind a recurring deliverable has to be right every time, not most of the time.

You bring real curiosity to the business behind the numbers. You do not just produce an analysis, you ask what it means and whether it should change how the business plans or decides.

You move comfortably between recurring, deadline-driven deliverables and more open-ended strategic analysis, and you know how to prioritize when both compete for your time.

You build trust across Finance and other teams by being accurate, responsive, and clear about what your analysis does and does not say. You take feedback well and ask questions up front rather than guessing.

WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

The focus areas below reflect the business’s current priorities. As with most roles on a growing team, they may change as those priorities evolve, and may also include support for strategic initiatives such as partnerships or M&A as they arise.

FP&A: Forecasting & Profitability

  • Support the development and maintenance of annual budgets and rolling forecasts.
  • Conduct budget-to-actual variance analysis and support profitability analysis across the business.
  • Build and maintain financial models to support business decisions, including scenario and sensitivity analysis, particularly through the use of AI tools.
  • Contribute datasets and analysis to board and executive reporting materials. Work closely with other members of the Finance team, including the Senior Financial & Systems Analyst, on shared data and reporting priorities.

Pricing & Gross Margin Analysis

  • Conduct gross margin analysis by product, segment, and customer cohort, and identify trends and margin improvement opportunities.
  • Support pricing strategy and annual price increase analysis, including modeling impact across customer segments, for new and existing product lines.
  • Partner with Billing and RevOps to validate pricing and margin data before it reaches leadership.

Commission Calculations

  • Support monthly/quarterly commission calculations for Sales, Partner, and Operations teams, including quality control checks prior to distribution.
  • Partner with Sales, RevOps, and Partner teams to ensure the data behind commission calculations, such as bookings, quotas, and contract terms, is accurate.
  • Investigate and resolve commission discrepancies as they arise.

Data & Systems

  • Partner with the Senior Financial & Systems Analyst on the data and systems behind the company’s business intelligence, recurring reporting, and general analysis efforts.
  • Automate recurring deliverables, such as commission calculations, to reduce manual, spreadsheet-based work over time.
  • Contribute to the infrastructure work, the “plumbing,” that keeps Finance’s data and systems running reliably via a company-wide data warehouse.
  • Help document the business logic behind recurring Finance calculations so it’s repeatable and scalable.
  • Build or maintain dashboards and reporting views that support recurring Finance deliverables.

Flag data quality issues upstream and work with the relevant team to fix them at the source.

Requirements

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
  • 1–3 years of proven work experience as a Financial Analyst, or in a similar FP&A, accounting, or business analysis role.
  • Strong Excel skills, including advanced formulas and financial modeling.
  • Working knowledge of SQL and curiosity to learn more.
  • Excellent analytical skills and comfort working with large, sometimes imperfect datasets.
  • Ability to present financial data clearly through reports, charts, and summaries for both financial and non-financial audiences.
  • Hands-on experience with financial or ERP systems.
  • Strong personal accountability for accuracy, particularly on recurring deliverables that affect employee pay.

Preferred

  • Experience with NetSuite or a similar ERP platform.
  • Experience with a cloud data warehouse platform (e.g., Snowflake) or BI/reporting tools (e.g., Power BI).
  • Prior experience with sales commission calculations, gross margin analysis, or pricing analysis.

THIS ROLE REPORTS TO

VP of Finance (Christian Ebersol).

METRICS OF SUCCESS

  • Accuracy & reliability: recurring deliverables are accurate and delivered on time, with minimal rework.
  • Analytical value: your analysis is trusted and used by Finance leadership and cross-functional partners in decision-making.
  • Cross-functional trust: partner teams across the business view Finance as a reliable, responsive partner.
  • Growth in scope: demonstrates readiness to take on broader financial planning and strategic analysis responsibilities within 12 to 18 months.

Benefits

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer
jobs.excerpt: The Mill Adventure is a scale-up with the ultimate mission of building awesome products that will change the way the iGaming industry operates.
jobs.description:
The Mill Adventure is a scale-up with the ultimate mission of building awesome products that will change the way the iGaming industry operates. We started our journey in 2019 with the vision of building a technology-driven organisation and creating a team consisting of the best of the best specialists in their respective fields.

Today, we provide a complete gaming platform for rapid deployment and success in iGaming. Our team of 100+ technology and iGaming experts is guided by a passion for invention, operational excellence and commitment to improving the inefficient.

We trust and value our team and strive to accommodate the right working conditions for each individual in remote, office-based or mixed models. We see the strength in being different and embracing the cultural diversity existing in our group.

One of our key strengths is our modern, event-driven, serverless technology stack, which allows us to innovate and move fast. We work in a collaborative environment that values both teamwork and autonomy.

The Role
As a Senior Security Engineer, you will be the cornerstone of our product and cloud security posture. You will own security across the code, the cloud, the pipelines, the corporate estate, and the response when an alert comes in.

This is a hands-on role with real architectural ownership. You will design our security controls and then build them — our security team is small, and you will be one of three people, so there is nobody to hand a design to. That cuts both ways: almost nothing stands between a good idea and it being live, and there is nowhere to hide if it doesn't get delivered. If your recent work has been mostly programme management, vendor oversight or reviewing other people's designs, this won't be the right fit.

Much of the work will also happen through other people. Security can't do everything alone, so you will spend real time with developers and architects — reviewing designs, threat modelling, coaching on secure practices — and your impact will be measured as much by what they build securely as by what you build yourself.

The role spans security engineering, IT security, security operations and a degree of offensive security. Breadth matters less as a checklist than as judgement: knowing which risks are real, which findings are noise, what to fix first, and — most importantly — what to automate so it stays fixed without anyone watching it.

You will be doing this in 2026, which means AI sits on both sides of the board. Attackers move faster and cheaper than they did two years ago, and the only realistic way for three people to cover this surface is to build AI into how the team works. You should already be doing this, not planning to.

On how we work: we review each other's work openly, and designs get challenged on their merits. We think that produces better security, and we'd expect you to challenge ours in the same way.

What You'll Do:

  • Architect and lead the design and implementation of security controls across our cloud infrastructure, applications and CI/CD pipelines — and build them yourself
  • Coach and mentor developers, engineers and architects on secure design, threat modelling and cloud security, so that security scales beyond the security team and becomes part of how we build
  • Own vulnerability management and our attack surface: know what is exposed, prioritise by real exploitability rather than scanner severity, and drive findings to closure with the teams that own them
  • Own the security of the SDLC by integrating and tuning SAST, DAST and SCA so that developers keep them enabled because the signal is worth the friction
  • Engineer and maintain our cloud security posture, primarily in AWS and Cloudflare — hardening configurations, automating compliance checks, and closing gaps before they are found for you
  • Own detection and response end to end: shape what we log and alert on, tune out the noise, investigate what is real, remediate it, and write up what happened
  • Architect and guide our IAM strategy, working with engineering to deliver least-privilege access for human and machine identities that teams don't route around
  • Test our own systems. Use offensive techniques against our infrastructure, applications and identity flows to validate that controls work and to decide what actually gets fixed first
  • Use AI as a force multiplier for a team that is small relative to its surface — agentic tooling for triage, code review, detection engineering, evidence collection and the automation of toil. You will also be the person who secures AI systems as we adopt them
  • Automate everything. If you would otherwise do it twice, automate it
  • Bring us the uncomfortable assessments — with a plan and a first PR attached

Requirements

  • 5+ years hands-on in a technical security engineering role, including time where you were the person accountable for the fix, not the person who raised the ticket. Expect to be asked what you built, what it prevented, and how you knew it worked
  • You design and you deliver. You can produce an architecture that survives review, and you have a track record of the things you designed actually going live
  • Judgement across security engineering, IT security, security operations and offensive security. We are not looking for equal depth in all four — we are looking for someone who can tell a real risk from a noisy one across all of them, and who automates the response rather than handling it manually each time
  • Deep AWS security: IAM, Organizations and SCPs, Security Hub, GuardDuty, WAF, plus Cloudflare. You can walk through how you would detect and contain a compromised role, not just describe what each service does
  • You write code that runs in production and that other people depend on — Python, Go, Bash, with TypeScript a major plus
  • Infrastructure as Code and its real failure modes: drift, over-permissive modules, secrets in state, pipeline privilege escalation
  • Vulnerability and attack surface management you have personally run — including the harder half, which is getting other teams to close things
  • Solid understanding of SIEM and detection engineering: what to collect, how to turn it into detections that fire on real activity, and how to keep false positives from burying the team
  • Detection and response you have personally done. You have investigated real alerts and written the post-incident review
  • Working offensive knowledge. You need not be a pentester, but you should be able to chain misconfigurations into a real attack path and explain why one finding matters more than fifty from a scanner
  • Practical use of AI in your security work today, not curiosity about it. Tell us what you have built or automated with it, where it failed you, and how you validate what it produces
  • A current, specific view on AI-driven threats — what has actually changed for defenders, and what you would do about it here
  • SDLC security: SAST, DAST and SCA that you have integrated and, more importantly, tuned well enough that developers didn't turn them off
  • The ability to work autonomously without going dark, and to work closely with engineers without friction. Both, not one
  • Comfort with open technical debate. You can have a design challenged in review, make your case, and move forward either way

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience with PCI DSS — scoping, control implementation and evidence — as something you have engineered towards, not only been audited against.
  • Experience building and maintaining a SIEM: pipelines, parsing, cost control, detection-as-code.
  • Serverless and event-driven architecture at scale.
  • iGaming, fintech or another regulated, high-value-target industry.
  • Corporate IT security: SSO and identity providers, MDM, SaaS security posture, third-party and vendor access.
  • Experience securing AI or agentic systems.
  • Security frameworks (NIST CSF, CIS Benchmarks, CSA CCM) used as tools to get work done rather than as the work itself.
  • Public artifacts: tools you have released, writeups, CVEs, CTF results, talks.
  • Certifications such as CISSP, AWS Certified Security or CEH are welcome, though demonstrated work weighs considerably more in our process

Benefits

  • A lean, focused company, offering a flexible working environment
  • The opportunity to work with and learn form a highly skilled, talented team
  • A great company culture, where accountability is innate, transparency is key and competency is virtue
  • Being part of a tight knit, caring community
  • Work equipment of your choice
  • Private health insurance
  • Learning budget
  • Company wide and team based get togethers

About World Business Lenders (www.wbl.com)

World Business Lenders (WBL) is proud to offer short-term, real estate-backed commercial loans to a diverse range of small and medium-sized businesses across the United States, especially those who may find it challenging to secure traditional financing.

Typically, the work schedule is from 9:00am to 6:00pm Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, though there might be times when additional hours are needed to meet business demands.

We’re looking for someone with strong communication skills in English, both spoken and written.

  • Please note that all resumes should be submitted in English.

About the Role

  • Manage condition clearing and documentation workflows.
  • Monitor pipeline progression and operational SLAs.
  • Ensure loan files meet quality and completeness standards.
  • Coordinate activities across underwriting, title, valuation, and closing.
  • Resolve operational bottlenecks and escalations.
  • Maintain workflow controls and process documentation.
  • Drive operational efficiency and service improvements.

Typical Day-to-Day :

The Processing Analyst's day is focused on moving assigned loan files forward, communicating with customers and internal teams, and making sure all required information and documentation is completed accurately and on time.

  • Daily
    • Review assigned files and prioritize urgent or time-sensitive items.
    • Contact customers and follow up on outstanding documents or information.
    • Review documents received and identify missing or inconsistent information.
    • Update loan files and notes with current status and next steps.
    • Respond to Underwriting requests and work on outstanding conditions.
    • Communicate with Sales regarding file status, issues, or delays.
    • Coordinate with Closing, Title, Valuation, Legal, or other teams as needed.
    • Provide customers with updates and explain outstanding requirements.
    • Monitor files for potential delays and take action or escalate when necessary.
  • Weekly
    • Review the full pipeline and prioritize files based on stage, urgency, and outstanding requirements.
    • Follow up on aging files and unresolved conditions.
    • Ensure files moving to Underwriting or Closing are complete and ready.
    • Review upcoming closings and confirm all required steps are on track.
    • Follow up on outstanding closing items, including signatures, verification, and insurance requirements.
    • Keep Sales and other relevant teams informed of material changes or expected delays.
    • Review personal performance against Processing SLAs and quality expectations.
    • Overall ownership: The Analyst is responsible for knowing the status of every assigned file, knowing what is outstanding, following up without being reminded, and keeping the file moving to the next stage.

Key Responsibilities:

  • The Processing Analyst owns assigned loan files from receipt through Underwriting and, for approved loans, through Closing.
  • Review files, contact customers, and conduct interviews to understand the business, property, ownership, debts, and loan purpose.
  • Identify potential eligibility, documentation, or other issues early and escalate when necessary.
  • Collect, review, and organize required business, legal, property, ownership, guarantor, and insurance documents.
  • Work closely with Underwriting to provide requested information and clear conditions.
  • Keep customers and Sales updated on file status, outstanding requirements, and material issues.
  • Coordinate with Closing, Title, Valuation, Legal, and other teams to keep files moving.
  • Manage required closing steps, including notary coordination, loan document execution, confirmation calls, final ID verification, and insurance updates.
  • Maintain accurate file records and follow up on outstanding items until resolved.
  • Meet established Processing SLAs, quality standards, and documentation requirements.

Key Internal & External Interactions

The Processing Analyst will work regularly with the following teams and individuals:

  • Customers: Collect required information and documents, conduct interviews, provide application updates, answer questions, and communicate next steps.
  • Sales: Receive new files, clarify information, provide status updates, and communicate material issues or delays.
  • Underwriting: Submit complete files, respond to questions, provide additional documentation, and clear conditions.
  • Closing & Title: Coordinate closing requirements, signing, notary arrangements, loan documents, and other closing-related items.

SaaS Revenue & Financial Analyst — Flosum

About Flosum

Flosum is a Salesforce-native platform company delivering enterprise-grade DevOps, data protection, and security solutions to some of the world's largest organizations. Our product portfolio spans Cloud DevOps, Data Migrator, Data Masking, Data Backup, Org Security, Cloud Trust Center, and Sandbox Synchronization — all built natively on the Salesforce platform. We serve enterprise customers across technology, energy, financial services, healthcare, and federal government. Flosum is a growth-stage company operating with the intensity and speed of a startup backed by the discipline of a mature operator.

The Role

We're hiring a SaaS Revenue & Financial Analyst who will own the measurement layer of our entire business. You will be the person who knows every number — ARR, net retention, expansion, churn, pipeline conversion, cost of acquisition, gross margin by product line, services margin, cash flow, and everything in between. You'll work across Salesforce (our CRM and billing system of record) and QuickBooks (our financial system) to build a unified, always-current picture of company performance.

This is not a reporting role. This is an analytical role where you connect revenue operations data to financial outcomes and surface the insights that drive decisions at the CEO level.

What You'll Own

You will build and maintain our SaaS metrics infrastructure — ARR waterfall, cohort retention analysis, revenue recognition schedules, deferred revenue tracking, and unit economics by segment. You will reconcile Salesforce bookings data against QuickBooks revenue entries and ensure we have a single source of truth across both systems. You will produce monthly and quarterly financial and revenue packages for leadership, including variance analysis against plan. You will model scenarios for pricing changes, product bundling, geographic expansion, and headcount investment. You will monitor pipeline health and translate pipeline data into revenue forecasts with documented assumptions. You will own the data integrity between our CRM and accounting systems, flagging discrepancies before they compound. You will support board-level and investor-level reporting with clean, defensible metrics.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

You have three-plus years of experience in SaaS financial analysis, revenue operations, or FP&A at a B2B software company. You are deeply proficient in Salesforce — not as a user, but as someone who understands opportunity objects, product schedules, contract structures, and reporting at a data level. You are equally proficient in QuickBooks Online, including chart of accounts design, revenue categorization, journal entries, and reconciliation workflows. You understand ASC 606 revenue recognition principles and can apply them to a multi-product SaaS business with annual and multi-year contracts. You can build financial models from scratch in Excel or Google Sheets — not from templates, from logic. You think in terms of cohorts, not just totals. You understand the difference between bookings, billings, and revenue, and you can explain why each matters. You are precise, skeptical of your own numbers, and obsessive about data integrity.

Preferred

Experience at a company with a mix of subscription revenue and professional services. Familiarity with Salesforce CPQ or native Salesforce quoting and contract objects. Exposure to investor or board reporting at a growth-stage company. Experience with Marketo or HubSpot data as it relates to CAC and attribution modeling.

Why Flosum

You'll report directly into the CEO's operating rhythm. Your work will not sit in a queue — it will shape hiring plans, product investment, and go-to-market strategy in real time. Flosum is building the definitive platform for Salesforce lifecycle management, and we need someone who can measure every dimension of that growth with precision.

We are a bootstrapped, profitable enterprise SaaS company at $30M ARR with a clear trajectory to $100M. This is a company built by missionaries, not mercenaries—and we expect the same from our CRO.

The Product Portfolio

Our platform consists of five integrated product lines, all built 100% natively within the Salesforce ecosystem. This native architecture is a core competitive differentiator—no external servers, no third-party middleware, no security exposure points:

  • DevOps — End-to-end release management, version control, CI/CD, and automated deployments for Salesforce environments. Designed for enterprise-scale complexity with full audit trails and compliance controls.
  • Backup & Archive — Complete data protection with automated backup scheduling, granular recovery, and intelligent archival capabilities that help enterprises manage data lifecycle and reduce storage costs.
  • Trust Center (Security & Compliance) — Proactive security scanning, vulnerability detection, and compliance monitoring that gives regulated enterprises real-time visibility into the health and security posture of their Salesforce environments.
  • Data Seeding — Intelligent test data management that enables enterprises to create realistic, anonymized datasets for sandbox and development environments without exposing production data.
  • DevOps for Veeva — Purpose-built release management for life sciences organizations running Veeva CRM on the Salesforce platform, addressing the unique regulatory and validation requirements of pharmaceutical and biotech companies.

The company has also integrated AI-powered capabilities into the platform, enabling intelligent automation across the DevOps lifecycle. The multi-product portfolio creates a powerful land-and-expand motion: the average deal size is increasing, and the cross-sell opportunity across the five product lines is substantial and largely untapped.

Requirements

Core Responsibilities

Revenue Strategy & Execution

  • Own the full revenue number: new business, expansion, renewal, and retention across all segments (Enterprise, Mid-Market, and emerging PLG).
  • Design and execute the go-to-market strategy to scale from $30M to $100M ARR within 3–4 years while maintaining profitability.
  • Build and operationalize a quarterly planning cadence with bottoms-up forecasting, pipeline coverage models, and segment-level unit economics tracking.
  • Establish minimum deal size thresholds and systematically prune low-value accounts that dilute team capacity and drag down margins.
  • Drive cross-sell and upsell motions across the five-product portfolio, increasing average contract value and multi-product adoption rates.

Pipeline & Demand Generation

  • Build a scalable, multi-channel demand generation engine spanning outbound prospecting, content marketing, digital campaigns, events, partner referrals, and product-led growth.
  • Own pipeline coverage ratios and ensure 3–4x pipeline-to-quota coverage at all times across segments.
  • Implement rigorous pipeline inspection and deal management processes with weekly forecasting reviews, stage-gate criteria, and data-driven coaching.
  • Personally engage in strategic pipeline development for enterprise accounts, including executive-to-executive relationship building.

Product-Led Growth & Innovation

  • Design and execute a PLG motion that creates a self-service entry point into the platform, converting free or low-cost users into enterprise contracts.
  • Build the instrumentation, analytics, and product-sales handoff processes required to identify and convert PLG-qualified leads into sales-assisted opportunities.
  • Develop innovative go-to-market strategies that differentiate the company from competitors relying on traditional sales motions, including community-led growth and ecosystem-based strategies.

Enterprise Sales & Large Deal Execution

  • Personally lead and close strategic enterprise deals with Fortune 500 accounts, particularly in regulated industries with complex procurement and compliance requirements.
  • Penetrate large enterprise accounts through multi-threaded relationships, executive sponsorship, and value-based selling that ties platform outcomes to business-critical KPIs.
  • Build and manage a structured enterprise deal process including discovery frameworks, mutual close plans, executive business reviews, and competitive displacement playbooks.
  • Develop an account-based strategy for the top 50 target accounts with dedicated pursuit plans, relationship maps, and executive engagement cadences.

Customer Retention & Expansion

  • Drive gross revenue retention from current levels to 92%+ through proactive customer health monitoring, risk identification, and executive intervention processes.

  • Establish executive-level relationships with top accounts, ensuring strategic alignment and long-term partnership positioning.
  • Implement a structured customer lifecycle management process from onboarding through renewal, with clear ownership, milestones, and escalation paths.

Global Team Leadership

  • Recruit, develop, and retain A-level talent across all revenue functions, with a particular emphasis on hiring missionaries who demonstrate ownership mentality and independent judgment.
  • Manage distributed teams across time zones with disciplined operating rhythms, clear communication protocols, and consistent performance management.

Unit Economics & Profitable Growth

  • Maintain and improve unit economics as the company scales: CAC payback under 18 months, LTV-to-CAC ratio above 3x, and gross margins consistent with best-in-class SaaS benchmarks.

jobs.description:
Location: 100% remote (EMEA)

Classification: Full-time

Pay Range: 82.000€ to 140.000€ - determined by several factors, including location

Miaplaza is dedicated to making education engaging and accessible through innovative online learning platforms. We develop personalized learning experiences for students, helping them grow in a supportive and interactive environment. Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive education curriculum platform where all students can be successful!

As an engineering manager at Miaplaza, your team will build technology with a direct impact on the lives of hundreds of thousands of students. Every step of the way, you will have the opportunity to influence our direction. Through our platforms, we create engaging, safe, and thoughtfully designed learning experiences that help children grow academically, creatively, and personally. Every feature we ship, every system we scale, and every improvement we make contributes to shaping how the next generation learns and discovers their potential. If our platform is down, a child might not go to school that day. We’re looking for leaders who want their work to matter in classrooms and homes, who care about access to quality education, and who are excited to craft technology that makes a difference in young people’s lives. Here, your impact doesn’t just power a product; it shapes future generations!

What you’ll work on:

We’re moving everything towards GCP and Kubernetes. We’re growing towards a scale that no longer matches our legacy architecture and actively investing in modernization. We’re migrating on-premise workloads to GKE, strengthening security and business continuity best practices, and moving toward platform self-service for our development teams. A core goal is to consolidate and shrink the stack, and every migration decision is measured against whether it lowers the daily burden on the team. You’ll need to work with your team balancing both platform initiatives and the operational needs of the engineering teams you serve. You’ll report to our head of engineering and be expected to split your time roughly 50/50 between people management and hands-on development. Prioritization always goes to leading and supporting your engineers. Your team will consist of four engineers.

What’s unique about management at Miaplaza:

Miaplaza is a US-based education company, which means we probably are doing things differently than you’ve done in your past experience. Here are a few differences you may notice:

  1. You will first onboard within your team as a senior engineer for 2 months. You will start to onboard as a manager during month two and will take over the team roughly at 10 weeks. This is non-negotiable as both periods of time are equally important.

  2. We expect our EMs to spend approximately 50% of their time hands-on, even after they’ve completed onboarding as a senior engineer.

  3. We emphasize the importance of pedagogical principles. A responsibility is to grow your engineers and those around you.

  4. One of such pedagogical principles is that we expect you to have full oversight into your direct reports' work; you can’t properly teach if you don’t see the process behind the output.

  5. Feedback is the norm. You’ll be expected to give meaningful, specific reinforcement and constructive feedback whenever you notice something. You should also expect to receive feedback. Ultimately, everything we do is optimizing ourselves, our teams, our processes, and our company to best support our students.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

  • 2+ years of experience being a mentor/leader, of which:

    • 1+ years leading a team, formally or as a tech lead

  • 7+ years of experience in DevOps, SRE, or Infrastructure Engineering, of which:

  • 3+ years running production workloads on Kubernetes (GKE preferred)

  • 3+ years of experience with a major cloud provider and Infrastructure as Code. GCP is our primary cloud and we expect senior-level knowledge of IAM, networking, KMS, GKE, CloudSQL and Secret Manager

  • 3+ years of experience operating at a Senior, Staff, or Principal Engineer level.

  • Experience with CI/CD pipeline design and operations

  • Experience with GitOps (FluxCD or ArgoCD)

  • Experience working directly with engineering teams and other managers as your customers on scoping and prioritization

  • Experience leading incident response, including running postmortems

What makes you stand out:

Experience leading a team through a significant architectural migration

Experience with consumer platforms at scale

Experience building in regulated environments

Experience operating self-hosted observability stacks (Prometheus, Thanos, Loki, Grafana, Tempo, OpenTelemetry)

Experience building internal developer platforms or self-service tooling

Experience supporting .NET/C# application deployments

Experience with database operations (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, RabbitMQ)

Experience with Istio or other service meshes

Responsibilities

  • Work with your team to design, build, and operate the infrastructure the rest of engineering depends on: clusters, pipelines, databases, edge, and observability

  • Your customers are the other engineering teams. Work with the other Engineering Managers and product development leadership to scope and prioritize platform work

  • Set the quality bar for your team. Lead by example.

  • Manage, lead, and mentor your team while working side by side with them in code quality, clean infrastructure-as-code, soft skills, best practices, etc

  • Lead team trainings, set SMART goals, hold performance reviews, and provide individual feedback recurrently to each of your devs

Our hiring process

As a remote company, we receive a large number of applicants, and finding the best fit for this role is our top priority — that’s why our process is longer than usual. At every stage, we try to be respectful of your time and grateful you’re spending it with us.

  • Application and CV Review - Our team will review your application responses and CV, then follow up with an update.

  • Initial Technical Screen (20 minutes) - A quick screening call to answer some administrative questions and confirm your basic technical knowledge. You'll be asked some administrative questions and 7 short technical questions related to the role.

  • Behavioral Interview (1 hour) - Meet with a member of our HR team to discuss your experience and share your approach throughout your career so far.

  • 1st Technical Interview (1 hour) - Meet with a member of the Infrastructure team to answer focused technical questions tailored to our work.

  • Scenario-based Technical Interview (1 hour) - Meet with a member of the Infrastructure team and the team's engineering manager to work through two hypothetical DevOps scenarios and how you would tackle them.

  • Leadership Interview (1 hour) - With our head of engineering and executive leadership.

  • Reference check - We'll reach out to the 3 references you provided, at least one being a former or current manager and any former or current direct reports.

  • Offer & background check - Once you sign your offer, we'll run a background check in accordance with applicable law.

We give honest, timely feedback at every step. Job searches are hard; we don't want to make yours harder.

Compensation and setup

The pay range for this role is €82,000 - 140,000. Miaplaza’s compensation philosophy ensures equity and competitiveness while considering regional differences in labor costs. Placement within a range is determined based on factors such as demonstrated skills, internal equity, and local labor market rates for the candidate’s geographic area.

Miaplaza is a growing, self-funded EdTech company. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. If you need accommodations at any point in the process, just let us know.

jobs.excerpt: QA Team LeadPosition OverviewCentrilogic is seeking to strengthen its quality assurance (QA) practice, which places testing professionals on client projects.
jobs.description:
QA Team Lead

Position Overview

Centrilogic is seeking to strengthen its quality assurance (QA) practice, which places testing professionals on client projects. To do that, we are looking for a QA Team Lead to run the QA workstream on those engagements. You will set the test approach, lead a team of QA Practitioners, and answer for the results of functional, regression, and user acceptance testing (UAT).

Our projects center on custom applications built on Azure and .NET, hosted in the cloud, on premises, or both. You will work alongside CentriLogic developers, business analysts, and project managers. Unit testing belongs to the development team and is outside the scope of this role.

We want thinkers as well as doers. You will question assumptions, look for better ways to test, and bring innovation to the work, including practical use of AI. You will also write automation and review AI-produced test assets yourself, while managing stakeholders, plans, and the performance of your team.

Key Responsibilities

Test strategy and delivery

  • Define the test strategy, scope, entry and exit criteria, and release readiness measures for each engagement, based on business requirements and risk.
  • Plan testing across environments hosted in Azure or on premises, including environment readiness, configuration, and test data.
  • Estimate and plan QA effort, assign work to Practitioners, and track progress against the project plan.
  • Oversee the design of functional and regression test suites, and decide which scenarios to automate and which to keep manual.
  • Plan and coordinate UAT with business users: prepare scripts and test data, run sessions, collect feedback, track defects to closure, and report readiness for acceptance.
  • Lead defect triage with developers, business analysts, and project managers.
  • Maintain traceability from requirements and user stories to test cases and defects.
  • Report status, risks, and quality metrics to stakeholders and to the engagement lead.

Test automation

  • Build and maintain an automation framework for web UI, API, and integration regression testing, using a modern framework such as Playwright, Selenium, or Cypress, in a language that suits the project such as C#. Set coding standards and reusable components.
  • Design API and integration tests for .NET services and the systems they connect to.
  • Integrate automated regression into continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, using tools such as Azure Pipelines, GitHub Actions, or similar. Where it helps, run suites in parallel on a cloud browser service.
  • Track flaky tests, find the cause, and keep the regression suite fast and trustworthy.

AI enabled QA

  • Set how the team uses AI in testing, and require human review of everything AI produces before it enters a test suite or a report.
  • Use AI assistants and agents, such as GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and the Playwright Test Agents, or other similar tools, to draft test plans, test cases, test data, and automation code from requirements and user stories.
  • Use AI to find gaps and ambiguity in requirements, summarize failed runs and defect patterns, and rank regression tests by the risk of each change.
  • Test AI features in the applications we build, and plan for answers that vary from run to run.
  • Check tests written by AI for accuracy, maintainability, and security. Keep confidential data, credentials, and personal information out of prompts and test files, and use only approved tools.

Innovation and leadership

  • Challenge the usual way of testing. Pilot new tools and AI techniques, measure whether they help, and share what works across the practice.
  • Coach and review the work of QA Practitioners, set goals, and give regular feedback.
  • Report on defect leakage, regression automation coverage, test stability, UAT completion, and release readiness.
  • Contribute to the CentriLogic QA practice with reusable templates, accelerators, estimating guidance, and QA input to proposals and statements of work.

Example Tools

The tools below are examples, not requirements. We welcome candidates with equivalent experience in other tools, and we choose tools engagement by engagement.

Area

Examples, or other similar tools

Test management and UAT

Azure DevOps Boards and Test Plans (cloud or Server), Jira with a test management add on, or other similar tools. Browser extensions for exploratory testing, such as Test & Feedback.

UI, API, and integration automation

Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, or other similar frameworks, in C#, TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, or Python. Postman, REST Assured, or other similar tools for API testing.

Pipelines and execution

Azure Pipelines, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or other similar tools, with cloud browser services such as Playwright Workspaces in Azure App Testing where parallel runs help.

AI support

GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, AI test agents such as the Playwright Test Agents, Model Context Protocol servers that connect assistants to a browser, or other similar tools.

Accessibility

Accessibility Insights for Web or other similar tools, checking against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 level AA.

Reporting

Azure DevOps dashboards, Power BI, Excel, or other similar tools.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in software QA, including at least 2 years leading a QA team or workstream.
  • Proven delivery of functional, regression, and UAT testing on custom enterprise applications, including web, API, and integration layers.
  • Experience testing applications built on Azure and .NET, hosted in the cloud, on premises, or both.
  • Hands on experience building test automation with a framework such as Playwright, Selenium, or Cypress, or a similar tool, in a language such as C#, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python.
  • Experience managing test cases, defects, and requirement traceability in a tool such as Azure DevOps Test Plans or Jira.
  • Experience running automated tests in CI/CD pipelines.
  • Has used generative AI in testing work, such as test design, test data, automation code, or defect analysis, and has sound judgment in reviewing its output.
  • A record of thinking differently: you have introduced a new tool, technique, or AI approach that improved how testing was done.
  • Clear written and spoken communication with executives, business users, and technical teams, including setting expectations and raising risks early.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with C# and the .NET ecosystem.
  • Experience testing applications that include AI features, such as chatbots or AI agents.
  • Accessibility testing experience.
  • International Software Testing Qualifications Board (ISTQB) certification, or a Microsoft certification relevant to Azure or DevOps.
  • Exposure to Microsoft Power Platform is an asset.
  • Experience at a consulting or professional services firm, and experience delivering work remotely across time zones.

What We're Looking For

We want a lead who thinks. You see a testing problem and ask whether there is a better way to solve it. You try new ideas, including AI, and you can show what worked and what did not. You can join a project, put a workable test approach in place quickly, and report results people trust. You will also help Practitioners build the same habits of curiosity and careful checking.
